definition_zh: 流动；流量；车流；源自
definition_en: to move steadily like water, or a steady movement or supply of something
core_image: 河水绕过石头，连成一条不停的线
scene: 河水缓缓流过石桥。 The river flows slowly under the stone bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 flow 是「流动」（第 1 个义项）；句意：河水缓缓流过石桥。

senses.title: Move like water
senses.definition: to move steadily in a stream
senses.definitionCN: 像水流一样稳定移动
senses.example: The river flows slowly under the stone bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 河水缓缓流过石桥。
senses.why: This is the core physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的物理义项。

senses.title: Steady movement
senses.definition: a continuous movement of people, goods, or information
senses.definitionCN: 人、货物或信息的持续移动
senses.example: The flow of traffic was heavy.
senses.exampleCN: 车流很密集。
senses.why: Water became a model for any continuous movement.
senses.whyCN: 水成为任何持续运动的模型。

senses.title: Arise from
senses.definition: to come from a source
senses.definitionCN: 从某个来源产生
senses.example: Many problems flow from poor planning.
senses.exampleCN: 许多问题源于计划不周。
senses.why: A river flows from its source, and so does a result.
senses.whyCN: 河流从源头流出，结果也从原因流出。

senses.title: Supply
senses.definition: the rate at which something is supplied
senses.definitionCN: 某物被供给的速率
senses.example: They measured the flow of water.
senses.exampleCN: 他们测量了水流量。
senses.why: The movement measured over time is a flow.
senses.whyCN: 随时间计量的运动就是流量。

intro.en: Flow comes from Old English flowan, a Germanic verb for moving like water.
intro.cn: flow 源自古英语 flowan，是日耳曼语中表示像水一样移动的动词。

items.en: The root meant to flow or stream.
items.cn: 这个词根意为流动或涌流。

items.en: Flowan meant to move like water.
items.cn: flowan 意为像水一样移动。

items.en: Flow also named a rising tide.
items.cn: flow 也指上涨的潮水。

items.en: The noun named a steady movement.
items.cn: 名词形式指稳定的运动。

items.en: The word extended to traffic, money, and ideas.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到交通、金钱和思想。

note.en: Flow is compared with similar-looking words and with words for moving liquid.
note.cn: 把 flow 与形近词以及表示液体运动的词作比较。

entries.definition: a fault or weakness
entries.definitionCN: 缺陷

entries.definition: past tense of fly
entries.definitionCN: 飞（过去式）

entries.definition: the surface of a room
entries.definitionCN: 地板

entries.definition: to flow steadily
entries.definitionCN: 流淌

entries.definition: to flow, as a tap does
entries.definitionCN: 流出

entries.definition: to flow quickly
entries.definitionCN: 倾泻

normalIntro.en: Flow is one continuous line of movement, of water, traffic, money, or causes.
normalIntro.cn: flow 是一条连续的运动线：水、交通、金钱或原因。

normal.en: The river flows to the sea.
normal.cn: 河流向大海。

normal.en: Traffic flows better after the fix.
normal.cn: 修复后车流更顺畅。

normal.en: Cash flow keeps a business alive.
normal.cn: 现金流让企业存活。

normal.en: Good results flow from good habits.
normal.cn: 好结果源于好习惯。

normal.en: The tide ebbs and flows.
normal.cn: 潮水涨落。

abstract.en: Water teaches that movement needs a channel.
abstract.cn: 水告诉我们运动需要通道。

abstract.en: Blocked flow builds pressure.
abstract.cn: 被阻断的流动会积聚压力。

abstract.en: Every result has a source upstream.
abstract.cn: 每个结果在上游都有源头。

examples.en: The river flows slowly under the stone bridge.
examples.cn: 河水缓缓流过石桥。

examples.en: The flow of traffic was heavy.
examples.cn: 车流很密集。

examples.en: Many problems flow from poor planning.
examples.cn: 许多问题源于计划不周。

dict_mnemonic.text: flow 源自古英语 flowan（流动），与 flood、fleet 同根，核心义「像水一样连续移动」。

root: 源自古英语 flowan（流动），核心义「连续不断的移动」。

sensesIntro.en: Flow means to move like water, a steady movement, a rate of supply, or to arise from.
sensesIntro.cn: flow 意为像水一样流动、持续运动、供给流量或源自某处。

core.en: Continuous movement along a course.
core.cn: 沿通道的连续运动。

branches.en: Water moving in a stream.
branches.cn: 在溪流中移动的水。

branches.en: Traffic or goods in motion.
branches.cn: 运动中的交通或货物。

branches.en: A result coming from a cause.
branches.cn: 由原因产生的结果。

branches.en: The measured rate of supply.
branches.cn: 计量出的供给速率。

branches.en: Rivers and reasons both have sources.
branches.cn: 河流与理由都有源头。

intro.en: Flow builds words for directions, instruments, and excess.
intro.cn: flow 构成表示方向、仪器和过量的词。

latinIntro.en: Flow has no Latin ancestor; Latin fluere, to flow, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: flow 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 fluere（流）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The river flowed over the bank.
The flowing water cut the stone.
The outflow of money worried them.

definition_zh: 范围；机会；观察仪器；仔细查看
definition_en: the range something covers, the chance to do something, a viewing instrument, or to examine something carefully
core_image: 地图上用铅笔圈出的区域，边界线清楚地把范围标出来
scene: 这项研究的范围只包括本地居民。 The scope of the study covers only local residents.
sceneCN: 这里 scope 是「范围」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这项研究的范围只包括本地居民。

senses.title: Range of coverage
senses.definition: the range of subjects or things something deals with
senses.definitionCN: 某事物所涉及的主题或事物的范围
senses.example: The question is beyond the scope of this book.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题超出了本书的范围。
senses.why: The central sense is the boundary of what is included.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是所涵盖内容的边界。

senses.title: Chance to act
senses.definition: the opportunity or freedom to do something
senses.definitionCN: 做某事的机会或自由空间
senses.example: There is scope for improvement.
senses.exampleCN: 还有改进的余地。
senses.why: A range of action becomes a chance within that range.
senses.whyCN: 行动范围变成范围内的机会。

senses.title: A viewing instrument
senses.definition: a device for looking at something, often in compounds
senses.definitionCN: 用于观察某物的装置，常作构词成分
senses.example: The doctor used a scope to see inside.
senses.exampleCN: 医生用内窥镜查看内部。
senses.why: The Greek root meant a watcher, so instruments of sight took the word.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根意为观看者，因此观察仪器用了这个词。

senses.title: To examine carefully
senses.definition: to look over something to learn about it
senses.definitionCN: 查看某物以了解它
senses.example: They scoped out the new office.
senses.exampleCN: 他们仔细察看了新办公室。
senses.why: The noun of range becomes a verb of surveying.
senses.whyCN: 表示范围的名词转为勘察的动词。

intro.en: Scope comes from Greek skopos, a watcher or target, through Italian scopo.
intro.cn: scope 源自希腊语 skopos（观看者、目标），经意大利语 scopo 进入英语。

items.en: Skopos meant a watcher or a mark to aim at.
items.cn: skopos 意为观看者或瞄准的目标。

items.en: Scopo meant aim or purpose.
items.cn: scopo 意为目标或目的。

items.en: Scope entered English meaning purpose or aim.
items.cn: scope 进入英语时意为目的或目标。

items.en: Scope came to mean the range of a subject.
items.cn: scope 开始表示主题的范围。

items.en: Scope also names viewing instruments and the act of surveying.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scope 还指观察仪器与勘察行为。

note.en: Scope is compared with similar-looking words and with words for range and room.
note.cn: 把 scope 与形近词以及表示范围和余地的词作比较。

entries.definition: a deep spoon, or a news story
entries.definitionCN: 勺子；独家新闻

entries.definition: a surface that rises or falls
entries.definitionCN: 斜坡

entries.definition: to reprove angrily
entries.definitionCN: 责骂

entries.definition: the limits between which something varies
entries.definitionCN: 范围

entries.definition: the size or degree of something
entries.definitionCN: 程度；范围

entries.definition: opportunity or space for something
entries.definitionCN: 余地；空间

normalIntro.en: Scope is the range you can see or reach, and also the instrument that helps you see.
normalIntro.cn: scope 是你能看到或触及的范围，也是帮助观看的仪器。

normal.en: The scope of a study is what it covers.
normal.cn: 研究范围就是它涵盖的内容。

normal.en: Scope for improvement means room to do better.
normal.cn: scope for improvement 意为改进余地。

normal.en: Telescope and microscope both end in scope.
normal.cn: telescope 与 microscope 都以 scope 结尾。

normal.en: To scope out a place is to look it over.
normal.cn: scope out 一个地方就是察看它。

normal.en: Beyond the scope means outside the limits.
normal.cn: beyond the scope 意为超出范围。

abstract.en: The Greek root joins watching with aiming.
abstract.cn: 希腊词根把观看与瞄准连在一起。

abstract.en: What you can see defines what you can do.
abstract.cn: 能看到的范围界定了能行动的范围。

abstract.en: Instruments of sight carry the name of the act of seeing.
abstract.cn: 观察仪器沿用「看」这一动作的名称。

examples.en: The question is beyond the scope of this book.
examples.cn: 这个问题超出了本书的范围。

examples.en: There is scope for improvement.
examples.cn: 还有改进的余地。

examples.en: They scoped out the new office.
examples.cn: 他们仔细察看了新办公室。

dict_mnemonic.text: scope 源自希腊语 skopos（观看者、目标），所以 telescope 是「看远处」，microscope 是「看微小」，scope 本身指「观察范围」。

root: 源自希腊语 skopos（观看者、目标），核心义「目光所及与目标所在的范围」。

sensesIntro.en: Scope means the range covered, the chance to act, a viewing instrument, or the act of examining.
sensesIntro.cn: scope 意为涵盖范围、行动余地、观察仪器，或仔细查看。

core.en: The field that sight or action can reach.
core.cn: 目光或行动能够到达的领域。

branches.en: The limits of what a subject includes.
branches.cn: 某个主题所包含的界限。

branches.en: The freedom to do something within limits.
branches.cn: 在界限内做某事的自由。

branches.en: A device that extends sight.
branches.cn: 延伸视力的装置。

branches.en: The act of looking something over.
branches.cn: 仔细察看某物的行为。

branches.en: A clear range creates a real chance to act.
branches.cn: 清晰的范围创造出真实的行动机会。

intro.en: Scope forms names for instruments of sight and for surveying.
intro.cn: scope 构成表示观察仪器与勘察的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Greek skopos passed through Italian scopo into English.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 skopos 经意大利语 scopo 进入英语。

items.example: Each team scopes its own area.
items.exampleCN: 每个小组察看自己的区域。

items.meaning: surveyed, or fitted with a scope
items.example: The scoped rifle lay on the table.
items.exampleCN: 带瞄准镜的步枪放在桌上。

items.example: Scoping the project took a week.
items.exampleCN: 界定项目范围花了一周。

items.meaning: an instrument for seeing small things
items.example: The cells are visible under a microscope.

items.meaning: an instrument for seeing distant things
items.example: They watched the stars with a telescope.
items.exampleCN: 他们用望远镜观察星星。

items.meaning: a tube for seeing above or around
a tube for seeing inside the body
to examine a place or plan
items.example: We scoped out the route first.

definition_zh: 抵抗；抵制；忍住
definition_en: to fight against something, or to stop yourself from doing something
core_image: 双手撑住一扇被猛推的门，不让它关上
scene: 居民联合起来反对在公园里建停车场。 Residents joined together to resist the plan for a car park in the park.
sceneCN: 这里 resist 是「抵制」（第 1 个义项：反对并试图阻止）；句意：居民联合起来抵制在公园里建停车场的计划。

senses.title: To fight against something
senses.definition: to act against a force, plan, or person that tries to control you
senses.definitionCN: 对试图控制你的力量、计划或人采取对抗行动
senses.example: Residents joined together to resist the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 居民联合起来抵制这项计划。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to stand against, and standing firm is the core image.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「站到对面」，站稳是核心意象。

senses.title: To refuse to accept
senses.definition: to refuse to accept a change, idea, or influence
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝接受某种变化、观念或影响
senses.example: Many staff resisted the new rules at first.
senses.exampleCN: 许多员工起初抗拒新规定。
senses.why: Standing against can be mental as well as physical.
senses.whyCN: 「站到对面」既可以是身体的，也可以是心理的。

senses.title: To stop yourself doing something
senses.definition: to stop yourself from doing something you want to do
senses.definitionCN: 阻止自己去做想做的事
senses.example: She could not resist the temptation to laugh.
senses.exampleCN: 她忍不住笑了出来。
senses.why: The urge is an inner push, and resisting is the self standing against it.
senses.whyCN: 冲动是一种内在推力，而抵抗就是自我顶住它。

intro.en: Resist comes from Latin resistere, to stand against, from re- and sistere, to take a stand.
intro.cn: resist 来自拉丁语 resistere（站到对面），由 re- 与 sistere（站定）构成。

items.en: Sistere means to cause to stand or take a stand.
items.cn: sistere 意为使站立、站定。

items.en: Resistere means to stand against or withstand.
items.cn: resistere 意为站到对面、抵挡。

items.en: Resister means to resist or oppose.
items.cn: resister 意为抵抗、反对。

items.en: Middle English resisten keeps the sense of standing firm.
items.cn: 中古英语 resisten 保留「站稳」的意思。

items.en: Resist covers both physical and moral opposition.
items.cn: 到 15 世纪，resist 兼指身体与道德上的对抗。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of resisting temptation.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「抵抗诱惑」的义项。

note.en: Resist is a standing-against verb, and it sits near its family and near verbs for opposing and withstanding.
note.cn: resist 是一个「站到对面」的动词，与自身词族以及表示反对和抵挡的动词相邻。

entries.definition: the act of resisting or a force against motion
entries.definitionCN: 抵抗；阻力

entries.definition: able to withstand something
entries.definitionCN: 有抵抗力的

entries.definition: a device that limits electric current
entries.definitionCN: 电阻器

entries.definition: to disagree with and try to stop something
entries.definitionCN: 反对

entries.definition: to be strong enough to bear a force
entries.definitionCN: 承受住；抵挡

entries.definition: to say that you will not do something
entries.definitionCN: 拒绝

normalIntro.en: Resist contains Latin sistere, to stand: to resist is to stand against pressure.
normalIntro.cn: resist 含有拉丁语 sistere（站）：抵抗就是顶着压力站稳。

normal.en: Re- means back or against, and sistere means stand.
normal.cn: re- 表示回或对抗，sistere 表示站。

normal.en: Resist change is a common phrase in organisations.
normal.cn: resist change 是组织中的常见说法。

normal.en: Resist temptation is the inner version of standing firm.
normal.cn: resist temptation 是「站稳」的内心版本。

normal.en: Resistance is the noun, and resistant is the adjective.
normal.cn: resistance 是名词，resistant 是形容词。

normal.en: Compare oppose: oppose can be verbal, while resist often involves action.
normal.cn: 对比 oppose：oppose 可以是口头的，resist 常涉及行动。

abstract.en: Picture both hands braced against a closing door.
abstract.cn: 想象双手撑住一扇正在关上的门。

abstract.en: Imagine feet planted while a crowd pushes forward.
abstract.cn: 想象双脚钉住，人群却往前推。

abstract.en: Think of a guard holding a rope taut.
abstract.cn: 想象守卫把绳子绷得笔直。

examples.en: Residents joined together to resist the plan.
examples.cn: 居民联合起来抵制这项计划。

examples.en: She could not resist the temptation to laugh.
examples.cn: 她忍不住笑了出来。

examples.en: The material resists heat well.
examples.cn: 这种材料很耐热。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re + sist」——站稳了往回顶，就是抵抗；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sistere（站定）→ resistere（站到对面）→ 古法语 resister → 中古英语 resisten → 现代英语 resist。

sensesIntro.en: The verb pictures standing against a push: against a plan, against an idea, and against one's own urge.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词描绘顶住推力：顶住计划、顶住观念，也顶住自己的冲动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: feet planted and hands braced against a push.
core.cn: 核心意象：双脚钉住，双手撑住一股推力。

branches.en: Acting against an external force is the core sense.
branches.cn: 对抗外部力量，是核心义项。

branches.en: Refusing a change is the mental form of standing firm.
branches.cn: 拒绝变化，是站稳的心理形式。

branches.en: Resisting an urge is standing against an inner push.
branches.cn: 忍住冲动，是顶住内在推力。

branches.en: A plan resisted in public and in private uses the same image.
branches.cn: 公开与私下抵制计划使用同一意象。

branches.en: Rejecting an idea and controlling an urge both require strength.
branches.cn: 拒绝观念与控制冲动都需要力量。

intro.en: Resist is a Latin verb carried through French, with English endings forming its modern family.
intro.cn: resist 是经法语传递的拉丁动词，现代词族由英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin sistere means to take a stand, and resistere means to stand against.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sistere 意为站定，resistere 意为站到对面。

items.example: Re- adds the sense of pushing back.
items.exampleCN: re- 增添「顶回去」的意思。

items.example: Resistere joins the prefix and the root.
items.exampleCN: resistere 把前缀与词根结合。

items.example: Resister carries the verb into French.
items.exampleCN: resister 把这个动词带入法语。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或动作的词尾

definition_zh: 积极的；肯定的；正面的；确凿的；阳性的；正的；正电的；原级
definition_en: optimistic or hopeful; expressing agreement or certainty; showing that something is present; (of a number or charge) above zero
core_image: 在一张横轴上，站在零点右边，并明确说「是」
scene: 即使被第三次拒绝，她依然保持积极。 She stayed positive even after the third rejection.
sceneCN: 这里 positive 是「心态积极的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：即使被拒三次，她仍然保持积极。场景要点：方向朝上、向前看、不垮；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 积极的；肯定的；确凿的；阳性的；正的
正面之处；正数；（摄影）正片

derivatives.zh: 实证主义（只承认可观察事实）
假定；提出（与 positive 同出 positus）

senses.title: Optimistic and hopeful
senses.titleCN: 积极的：朝好处看的那种劲头
senses.definition: expecting good things and focusing on what can go well
senses.definitionCN: 期待好事、把注意力放在能顺利之处
senses.example: She stayed positive even after the third rejection.
senses.exampleCN: 即使被拒三次，她仍然保持积极。
senses.why: The word's core is 'laid down, definite'. A positive mind is one that has settled on the good outcome rather than leaving it open.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心是“被确定下来”。积极的心态，就是把结果定在好处上，而不是让它悬着。

senses.title: Expressing agreement or yes
senses.definition: expressing agreement, approval, or an affirmative answer
senses.definitionCN: 表达同意、赞许或肯定回答
senses.example: We received a positive reply within a day.
senses.exampleCN: 我们一天之内就收到了肯定的答复。
senses.why: A positive answer is one that has been fixed: not maybe, not pending, but settled in the affirmative.
senses.whyCN: 肯定的回答是被固定下来的回答：不是也许，不是待定，而是定在“是”这一边。

senses.title: Good or beneficial in effect
senses.titleCN: 正面的：带来好结果的那一面
senses.definition: producing a good or useful effect
senses.definitionCN: 产生良好或有用的效果
senses.example: The new bus route had a positive impact on local shops.
senses.exampleCN: 新公交线路对本地商铺产生了正面影响。
senses.why: What is settled and real tends to be counted on the good side. Positive becomes the label for effects we want more of.
senses.whyCN: 被确定、被落实的东西往往被算在好的一边。positive 成了“我们希望更多”的效果的标签。

senses.title: Definite and undeniable
senses.titleCN: 确凿的：摆在那里，不容否认
senses.definition: clear, definite, and not open to doubt
senses.definitionCN: 清楚、确定、不容怀疑
senses.example: We have positive proof that the letter was forged.
senses.exampleCN: 我们有确凿证据证明这封信是伪造的。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: in law, positive meant formally laid down. What is laid down is not a matter of opinion.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：在法律上，positive 指正式规定下来的。被规定下来的，就不是意见问题。

senses.title: Medical: showing the condition is present
senses.titleCN: 阳性的：查出了那个东西
senses.definition: showing that a particular substance, infection, or condition is present in a test
senses.definitionCN: 表示在检测中发现某种物质、感染或状况确实存在
senses.example: He tested positive for the virus but had no symptoms.
senses.exampleCN: 他的病毒检测呈阳性，但没有症状。
senses.why: A test is a yes-or-no question put to the body. Positive means the thing asked about is definitely there, not absent.
senses.whyCN: 检测是向身体提出的一个是非题。positive 表示所问之物确实存在，而非缺席。

senses.title: Mathematics: above zero
senses.definition: of a number, greater than zero
senses.definitionCN: 指数值大于零
senses.example: Multiplying two negative numbers gives a positive result.
senses.exampleCN: 两个负数相乘得到正数结果。
senses.why: On a number line, positive marks the direction that counts upward from zero. The sign is a settled direction.
senses.whyCN: 在数轴上，正号标记从零点向上计数的方向。这个符号是一个确定下来的方向。

senses.title: Physics: carrying positive charge
senses.titleCN: 正电的：与电子相反的那种电荷
senses.definition: having the kind of electric charge carried by protons, opposite to that of electrons
senses.definitionCN: 带有质子所携的那种电荷，与电子所带电荷相反
senses.example: The positive terminal is marked with a plus sign.
senses.exampleCN: 正极用加号标出。
senses.why: Franklin's convention named one kind of charge positive, and the label stuck. It is a naming decision, not a claim about which charge is better.
senses.whyCN: 富兰克林的约定把其中一种电荷命名为 positive，这个叫法沿用至今。它是命名决定，并不表示哪种电荷“更好”。

senses.title: Grammar: the base degree
senses.definition: in grammar, the simple form of an adjective or adverb, before comparison
senses.definitionCN: 语法上指形容词或副词未作比较的简单形式
senses.example: Good is the positive degree; better and best are the comparative and superlative.
senses.exampleCN: good 是原级；better 与 best 分别是比较级和最高级。
senses.why: The base form states a quality outright, with nothing added. It is the form laid down before any comparison modifies it.
senses.whyCN: 原级直接陈述一种性质，不加任何东西。它是任何比较来改动之前就已定下的形式。

intro.en: Positive comes from a Latin adjective meaning 'settled by agreement'. Its history runs from law to logic to mathematics to electricity, and only recently to optimism.
intro.cn: positive 来自一个意为“经约定确定下来”的拉丁形容词。它的历史从法律走到逻辑、数学、电学，而“乐观”这一义其实很晚才出现。

items.en: Ponere meant 'to put, place'. Its past participle positus, 'placed, set down', is the stem of the whole family: position, deposit, compose, positive.
items.cn: ponere 意为“放置”。其过去分词 positus“被放置的、被定下的”，是整个词族的词干：position、deposit、compose、positive。

items.en: Positivus meant 'settled by agreement, conventional'. In medieval law it described rules laid down by authority, as opposed to natural law.
items.cn: positivus 意为“经约定确定的、约定俗成的”。在中世纪法律中，它指由权威制定下来的规则，与自然法相对。

items.en: English positive appears in the 14th century first in legal and philosophical writing, with the sense 'formally laid down, absolute'.
items.cn: 英语 positive 于 14 世纪出现，最早见于法律与哲学写作，意为“正式规定的、绝对的”。

items.en: By the 15th and 16th centuries it means 'definite, not open to doubt', and it also enters grammar for the uncompared degree of an adjective.
items.cn: 到 15、16 世纪，它表示“确定的、不容怀疑”，并进入语法，指形容词未作比较的原级。

items.en: From the 18th century the word labels the direction above zero and, after Franklin, the kind of electric charge called positive. Photography later adds the positive image.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪起，这个词标记零点以上的方向；在富兰克林之后，又标记被称为正的那种电荷。摄影随后又加上“正片”。

items.en: The everyday sense 'hopeful, optimistic' is a 20th-century development. It is the newest layer and is not found in the older legal or scientific uses.
items.cn: “充满希望、乐观”的日常义是 20 世纪的产物。它是最新的一层，在较早的法律或科学用法中找不到。

note.en: The first group is built on the same Latin participle. The second group collects words for approval, certainty, and good effect.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一个拉丁分词上。第二组收表示赞同、确定与良好效果的词。

entries.definition: in a positive way, or absolutely. It also serves as an intensifier: positively dangerous means definitely dangerous.
entries.definitionCN: 以积极的方式，或绝对地。它也用作强调词：positively dangerous 意为“绝对危险”。

entries.definition: to suggest or assume something as a fact. It comes from Latin positus, the same participle behind positive.
entries.definitionCN: 提出或假定某事为事实。它来自拉丁 positus，即 positive 背后的同一个分词。

entries.definition: a place or a point of view. From positio, a noun built on the same participle positus.
entries.definitionCN: 位置或观点。来自 positio，由同一个分词 positus 构成的名词。

entries.definition: the antiparticle of the electron, with positive charge. Formed in the 1930s from positive plus electron.
entries.definitionCN: 电子的反粒子，带正电。20 世纪 30 年代由 positive 与 electron 拼合而成。

entries.definition: expecting good outcomes. Optimistic is narrower than positive, which also covers agreement, proof, and electric charge.
entries.definitionCN: 期待好结果。optimistic 比 positive 窄，后者还覆盖赞同、证据与电荷。

entries.definition: saying yes or giving support. Affirmative matches sense 02 and is the formal opposite of negative.
entries.definitionCN: 说“是”或给予支持。affirmative 对应第 2 义项，是 negative 的正式反义。

entries.definition: sure about oneself or an outcome. Confident describes the feeling; positive can describe both the feeling and the evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 对自己或结果有把握。confident 描述感受；positive 既可指感受，也可指证据。

entries.definition: helpful and intended to improve something. Constructive fits sense 03 and stresses usefulness rather than mood.
entries.definitionCN: 有益且意在改进的。constructive 对应第 3 义项，强调有用性而非情绪。

entries.definition: clear and certain. Definite matches sense 04 and is close to the older core of positive.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚而确定的。definite 对应第 4 义项，贴近 positive 较古老的核心义。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the plus side of the axis, the firm yes, the proof on the table, the test result, and the uncompared adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：轴的正侧、干脆的“是”、桌上的证据、化验结果、未作比较的形容词。

normal.en: Positive is the plus side: on a number line it points right, and in mood it points up.
normal.cn: positive 是加号那一边：在数轴上指向右，在心情上指向上。

normal.en: A positive answer is a yes that has been nailed down, not a maybe.
normal.cn: 肯定的答复是被钉死的“是”，不是“也许”。

normal.en: Positive proof is evidence placed on the table where nobody can talk it away.
normal.cn: 确凿证据就是摆到桌上、谁也说不掉的证据。

normal.en: A positive test means the thing you asked about is definitely there, like a light turning on.
normal.cn: 阳性检测意味着你问的那个东西确实在，就像一盏灯亮了。

normal.en: In grammar the positive degree is the plain form before any comparison touches it.
normal.cn: 语法上的原级，就是任何比较来碰它之前的朴素形式。

abstract.en: Positive originally meant settled by authority, not cheerful; the modern smile is a late guest in an old legal house.
abstract.cn: positive 本指“由权威定下”，并非“愉快”；现代的笑脸是这座古老法律宅子里晚来的客人。

abstract.en: A plus sign is a decision about direction, not a discovery about value.
abstract.cn: 加号是关于方向的决定，而不是关于价值的发现。

abstract.en: To call evidence positive is to say the question is closed; that is why the word can sound both reassuring and dangerous.
abstract.cn: 把证据称为 positive，等于宣布问题已经关闭；所以这个词听上去既可让人安心，也可让人警觉。

examples.en: The study found a positive correlation between sleep and test scores.
examples.cn: 这项研究发现睡眠与考试成绩之间存在正相关。

examples.en: Two of the samples tested positive for the bacteria.
examples.cn: 其中两份样本的细菌检测呈阳性。

examples.en: Try to frame the feedback in positive terms before listing the problems.
examples.cn: 在列举问题之前，尽量用正面措辞来组织反馈。

dict_mnemonic.text: “剖则提夫”——把好处剖出来、提出来给大家看，就是 positive（积极的、正面的）

root: 拉丁语 ponere“放置”的过去分词 positus → positivus“经约定确定的” → 英语 positive（14 世纪，先用于法律与哲学）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is 'settled, laid down'. A settled answer is affirmative; settled evidence is proof; a settled direction on the axis is plus; a settled charge is positive; a settled outlook is optimism. The grammatical sense is simply the form before comparison.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是“被确定、被定下”。确定下来的回答是肯定；确定下来的证据是确凿；轴上确定下来的方向是正；确定下来的电荷是正电；确定下来的看法是乐观。语法义则只是比较之前的形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark placed firmly on the plus side of a line, with nothing left open.
core.cn: 核心意象：在一条线的正侧牢牢按下记号，不留任何悬而未决。

branches.en: CERTAINTY: the firm yes and the proof that closes the question.
branches.cn: 确定：干脆的“是”，以及关闭问题的证据。

branches.en: VALUE: the hopeful outlook and the good effect it expects.
branches.cn: 价值：乐观的心态，以及它所期待的良好效果。

branches.en: DIAGNOSIS: the test that finds the thing present.
branches.cn: 诊断：查出某物确实存在的检测。

branches.en: SIGN: the plus side of the number line and of the electric charge.
branches.cn: 符号：数轴与电荷的正侧。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: the plain degree, stated before any comparison.
branches.cn: 语法：任何比较之前的朴素级。

intro.en: Positive is built from a Latin participle plus the adjective ending -ivus. The same stem, with different prefixes, yields most of the place-and-state vocabulary of English.
intro.cn: positive 由一个拉丁分词加形容词词尾 -ivus 构成。同一个词干配上不同前缀，产出了英语里大量表示“放置与状态”的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin positus is the pivot: every word below either contains it or is built by adding a prefix to the verb it comes from.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 positus 是枢纽：下面每个词要么含有它，要么是在其来源动词上加前缀构成。

senses.title: A natural moon
senses.definition: a natural body that orbits a planet
senses.definitionCN: 围绕行星运行的天体
senses.example: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite.
senses.exampleCN: 月球是地球唯一的天然卫星。
senses.why: The base sense is a smaller body circling a larger one.
senses.whyCN: 基础义是围绕更大天体运行的小天体。

senses.title: A man-made orbiter
senses.definition: a machine sent into orbit around the Earth or another body
senses.definitionCN: 被送入地球或其他天体轨道的装置
senses.example: The satellite sends weather data every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗卫星每小时传送一次气象数据。
senses.why: Technology copies the motion of a natural moon.
senses.whyCN: 技术复制了天然卫星的运行方式。

senses.title: A dependent place
senses.definition: a town or country that depends on a larger one nearby
senses.definitionCN: 依附于附近更大城镇或国家的城镇或国家
senses.example: The factory town became a satellite of the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 这座工厂城镇成了首都的卫星城。
senses.why: The image of circling around a centre extends to politics and cities.
senses.whyCN: 围绕中心的意象延伸到政治与城市。

entries.definition: to come to rest or agree

entries.definition: humour that mocks faults

entries.definition: to greet with respect
entries.definitionCN: 致敬

entries.definition: a natural body orbiting a planet
entries.definitionCN: 卫星；月亮

entries.definition: a vehicle designed for space

entries.definitionCN: 轨道飞行器

abstract.cn: 想象一名卫兵始终走在国王身旁。

sensesIntro.en: Satellite is a natural moon, a man-made orbiter, or a dependent place.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a smaller body circling a larger one.

branches.en: The base sense is a natural body in orbit.

branches.en: Natural moons and machines both orbit planets.

intro.en: Satellite combines with nouns to name space technology and dependent places.
intro.cn: satellite 与名词组合，指太空技术与依附性地方。

latinIntro.en: Latin satelles and its genitive satellitis are the source of satellite.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 satelles 及其属格 satellitis 是 satellite 的源头。

sceneCN: 这里 sharp 是「锋利的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这把刀很锋利，切菜很快。

senses.title: Fine edge
senses.definition: having an edge that cuts easily
senses.definitionCN: 刀刃容易切割的

senses.exampleCN: 这把刀很锋利，切菜很快。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.

senses.title: Quick to notice

senses.title: Sudden and large

normalIntro.cn: sharp 是一条细刃：切食物、切开困惑、截断变化、精确切定时间。

normal.en: Use a sharp knife.

normal.en: Prices took a sharp turn.
normal.cn: 价格急剧转向。

examples.en: She has a sharp mind.
examples.cn: 她头脑敏锐。

examples.en: The meeting starts at nine sharp.
examples.cn: 会议九点整开始。

dict_mnemonic.text: sharp 源自古英语 scearp（锋利），核心义「边缘细而能切」，由刀锋引申为思维敏锐、变化急剧与时间精确。

root: 源自古英语 scearp（锋利、尖利），核心义「能切开的细边」。

sensesIntro.en: Sharp means having a fine edge, quick in thought, sudden and large, or exactly on time.
sensesIntro.cn: sharp 意为锋利的、思维敏锐的、急剧的或正好准时的。

core.en: A narrow edge that cuts.
core.cn: 能切割的狭窄边缘。

branches.en: A blade that cuts easily.
branches.cn: 容易切割的刀刃。

branches.en: A mind that cuts to the point.
branches.cn: 能切中要害的头脑。

branches.en: A change with a steep edge.
branches.cn: 带有陡峭边缘的变化。

branches.en: A time cut with no margin.
branches.cn: 没有余量地切定时间。

branches.en: Blades and minds are both called sharp.
branches.cn: 刀刃与头脑都被称为 sharp。

intro.en: Sharp builds words for comparison, sharpening, and keen sight.
intro.cn: sharp 构成表示比较、磨利和目光敏锐的词。

latinIntro.en: Sharp has no Latin ancestor; Latin acutus, sharp, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: sharp 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 acutus（尖锐的）只是语义对应词。

items.example: It is the sharpest tool here.
items.exampleCN: 这是这里最锋利的工具。

items.example: The sharpness of the turn surprised us.

items.exampleCN: 一名目光敏锐的警卫看见了他。

definition_zh: 感谢；多谢；致谢
definition_en: an expression of gratitude, or because of someone
core_image: 一声随口递出的口头谢礼
scene: 他把伞递了过来。 Thanks for the umbrella.
sceneCN: 这里 thanks 是「多谢」（第 1 个义项）；句意：多谢你的伞。

derivatives.zh: thankful 加 -ly，义为「幸好；感激地」

senses.title: An expression of gratitude
senses.definition: a polite word showing you are grateful
senses.definitionCN: 表达感激的礼貌用语
senses.example: Thanks for the umbrella.
senses.exampleCN: 多谢你的伞。
senses.why: The plural of thank became a standing polite formula.
senses.whyCN: thank 的复数形式固化为常用的客套语。

senses.title: Credit due to someone
senses.definition: who or what made something happen, as in thanks to
senses.definitionCN: 促成某事的人或原因，如 thanks to
senses.example: Thanks to the rain, the crops survived.
senses.exampleCN: 多亏那场雨，庄稼活了下来。
senses.why: Gratitude points at its cause, so the phrase names the reason.
senses.whyCN: 感激指向原因，短语由此用来指明缘由。

intro.en: Thanks is the old plural of thank, fixed as a polite word.
intro.cn: thanks 是 thank 的古老复数，固定为礼貌用语。

items.en: Þank- meant a good thought of someone.
items.cn: 日耳曼词根 þank- 意为对某人的善念。

items.en: Þanc meant thought, favor and gratitude.
items.cn: 古英语 þanc 兼指想法、恩惠与谢意。

items.en: Thanks became the standing plural form.
items.cn: 中古英语 thanks 成为固定复数。

items.en: Thanks to developed for naming causes.
items.cn: 16 世纪 thanks to 用于点明缘由。

items.en: The interjection use is now the most common.
items.cn: 现代最常用作感叹语。

note.en: Thanks is compared with look-alike words and with gratitude words.
note.cn: 把 thanks 与形近词及致谢用词作对比。

entries.definition: the verb it comes from
entries.definitionCN: 其动词原形

entries.definition: considers, third person
entries.definitionCN: 思考（三单）；只是拼写相近

entries.definition: not a standard word
entries.definitionCN: 非标准拼写；仅形近

entries.definition: a fuller polite formula
entries.definitionCN: 更完整的客套语

entries.definition: formal gratitude
entries.definitionCN: 正式的谢意

entries.definition: the feeling of being grateful
entries.definitionCN: 感激之情

normalIntro.en: Thanks is the little verbal coin passed every day.
normalIntro.cn: thanks 是每天递出的口头小硬币。

normal.en: Thanks for the umbrella.
normal.cn: 多谢你的伞。

normal.en: Thanks to the rain, the crops survived.
normal.cn: 多亏那场雨，庄稼活了下来。

normal.en: Many thanks for your letter.
normal.cn: 非常感谢你的来信。

normal.en: She gave thanks before the meal.
normal.cn: 饭前她做了感恩祷告。

normal.en: It finished late, no thanks to the traffic.
normal.cn: 收尾很晚，这可怪不了交通。

abstract.en: A smile packed into two small words.
abstract.cn: 两个小字装下的一个微笑。

abstract.en: Gratitude turned into a habit.
abstract.cn: 感激变成了习惯。

abstract.en: Every gift deserves a coin of words.
abstract.cn: 每份馈赠都值得一枚言语的硬币。

examples.en: Thanks for the umbrella.
examples.cn: 多谢你的伞。

examples.en: Thanks to the rain, the crops survived.
examples.cn: 多亏那场雨，庄稼活了下来。

examples.en: Many thanks for your letter.
examples.cn: 非常感谢你的来信。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「谢克斯」——谢意带个复数尾巴「克斯」，一点小事也要「谢」，就是多谢。

root: 古英语 þanc（善念、谢意）的复数 þancas 经中古英语固化，成为现代的礼貌用语 thanks。

sensesIntro.en: Thanks speaks gratitude politely and names the cause behind events.
sensesIntro.cn: thanks 以礼道谢，并指明事情背后的缘由。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spoken coin of gratitude.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚说出口的感激硬币。

branches.en: The polite word is the daily coin.
branches.cn: 礼貌用语是日常硬币。

branches.en: Both senses credit a source.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把功劳归于来源。

branches.en: Thanks to names the reason.
branches.cn: thanks to 点明原因。

branches.en: No thanks to denies the credit.
branches.cn: no thanks to 拒绝归功。

branches.en: Giving thanks is the ritual coin.
branches.cn: give thanks 是仪式化的硬币。

intro.en: Thanks shows plural -s fixing a polite formula.
intro.cn: thanks 展示复数 -s 固化客套语。

latinIntro.en: Thanks comes from Germanic roots, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: thanks 源自日耳曼语源，并非拉丁语。

items.exampleCN: 确实是个吃力不讨好的任务。

definition_zh: 文化的；与文化有关的
definition_en: relating to the way of life, art, and beliefs of a group of people
core_image: 一条老街上，戏台、书店和庙挤在同一条巷子里
scene: 老街上戏台、书店和庙挤在一条巷子里，都是这座城的样子。 The festival is the cultural heart of the town.
sceneCN: 这里 cultural 指「文化的」（第 1 个义项：与一个群体的生活方式、艺术和信仰有关）；句意是这个节庆是这座镇的文化核心。

senses.title: Of a way of life
senses.definition: relating to the customs and beliefs of a group
senses.definitionCN: 与一个群体的习俗和信仰有关的
senses.example: Food is a cultural matter, not just a physical one.
senses.exampleCN: 饮食是文化问题，不只是生理问题。
senses.why: What a group repeats becomes its way of life.
senses.whyCN: 一个群体反复做的事，就成了它的生活方式。

senses.title: Of art and learning
senses.definition: relating to art, music, books, and learning
senses.definitionCN: 与艺术、音乐、书籍和学问有关的
senses.example: The city offers many cultural events.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市有很多文艺活动。
senses.why: A society keeps its best made things on show.
senses.whyCN: 一个社会把做得最好的东西摆出来给人看。

senses.title: Of refined taste
senses.definition: showing refined taste and education
senses.definitionCN: 表现出修养与教育的
senses.example: She moves in cultural circles.
senses.exampleCN: 她出入有文化气息的圈子。
senses.why: Training of the mind leaves a visible mark.
senses.whyCN: 心智受过训练，会留下看得见的痕迹。

intro.en: Cultural is Latin cultura, tilling, plus -alis, belonging to; English formed it in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: cultural 由拉丁语 cultura（耕种）加 -alis（属于）构成，十九世纪在英语中成形。

items.en: Cultura meant tilling the soil and giving care.
items.cn: cultura 指耕种土地并加以照料。

items.en: -Alis meant belonging to or relating to.
items.cn: -alis 意为属于或关于。

items.en: Cultural first meant of cultivation, of land or mind.
items.cn: cultural 最初指耕种或心智培养的。

items.en: It shifted to the arts and way of life of a people.
items.cn: 它转向一个群体的艺术与生活方式。

items.en: It now covers food, dress, music, and belief.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖饮食、服饰、音乐与信仰。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cult- stem, and the meaning group names other words for social life and taste.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cult- 词干，近义组列出其他关于社会生活与品味的说法。

entries.definition: the way of life of a people
entries.definitionCN: 一个群体的生活方式

entries.definition: trained and refined
entries.definitionCN: 受过训练而文雅的

entries.definition: a small group with strong beliefs
entries.definitionCN: 信念强烈的小团体

entries.definition: of art and its making
entries.definitionCN: 关于艺术及其创作的

entries.definition: of people living together
entries.definitionCN: 关于人共同生活的

entries.definition: polished in manner and taste
entries.definitionCN: 举止与品味经过打磨的

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a narrow street holding a stage and a temple and end with a trained eye.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一条挤着戏台与庙的窄巷开始，落到一双受过训练的眼睛。

normal.en: Culture plus -al makes an adjective about a whole way of life.
normal.cn: culture 加 -al，成了描述整套生活方式的形容词。

normal.en: A festival can be the heart of a town.
normal.cn: 一个节庆可以是一座镇的心脏。

normal.en: Cultural things are learned from others, not carried in blood.
normal.cn: 文化的东西是向别人学来的，不写在血里。

normal.en: Food, dress, and songs all carry culture.
normal.cn: 饮食、服饰与歌都带着文化。

normal.en: A cultured person shows what a culture trained.
normal.cn: 有修养的人，显出文化训练过的痕迹。

abstract.en: Picture a stage lit beside a small bookshop.
abstract.cn: 想象一座亮着灯的戏台挨着小小书店。

abstract.en: Picture hands passing food across a long table.
abstract.cn: 想象一双手把食物递过长桌。

abstract.en: Picture a child copying a dance step.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子跟着学舞步。

examples.en: The two countries began a cultural exchange.
examples.cn: 两国开始了文化交流。

examples.en: Old songs are part of our cultural heritage.
examples.cn: 老歌是我们文化遗产的一部分。

examples.en: The town has a busy cultural life.
examples.cn: 这镇的文化生活很热闹。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cultural 记成「种出来的」：culture 原是耕种，一个群体长期养出的习惯与艺术，就是文化。

root: 由拉丁语 cultura（耕种、照料）加形容词后缀 -alis 构成；十九世纪进入英语，本义与栽培有关，后指一个群体的艺术、信仰与生活方式。

sensesIntro.en: From a group's way of life, to its arts, to a refined manner.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个群体的生活方式，到它的艺术，再到文雅的举止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stage, a bookshop, and a temple in one narrow street.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条窄巷里同时有戏台、书店和庙。

branches.en: Customs shared by a group are called cultural.
branches.cn: 一个群体共享的习俗被称为文化的。

branches.en: Art and learning are the visible face of that life.
branches.cn: 艺术与学问是这种生活看得见的脸。

branches.en: A trained taste shows culture in one person.
branches.cn: 受过训练的品味，把文化显在一个人身上。

branches.en: A way of life and its art cannot be separated.
branches.cn: 生活方式与它的艺术分不开。

branches.en: What a society makes, a person can learn to love.
branches.cn: 社会做出来的东西，个人可以学着去爱。

intro.en: Cultural sits in the Latin cultura family, with culture, cultured, and agriculture around it.
intro.cn: cultural 属于拉丁语 cultura 一族，周围有 culture、cultured 与 agriculture。

latinIntro.en: The Latin cultura, tilling, is the root that carries -al into cultural.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cultura（耕种）是把 -al 带进 cultural 的根。

items.exampleCN: 从文化上说，这两座镇不同。
伦敦是座多元文化城市。
社会与文化的力量塑造品味。

definition_zh: 区；地区
definition_en: an area of a town or country with its own name, border or purpose
core_image: 老城地图上被街道围出的一小块，边线像铅笔轻轻描过
scene: 地图上用铅笔围出一小块，四条街正好当边。 The old district keeps its narrow lanes.
sceneCN: 这里 district 指「城区」（第 1 个义项：城市里划分出的一片区域）；句意是老城区保留着窄巷。

senses.title: A part of a town
senses.definition: a part of a city or town, often with its own name or character
senses.definitionCN: 城市里的一片地方，常有自己的名字或特点
senses.example: They moved to a quiet district near the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们搬到河边一个安静的城区。
senses.why: A city becomes readable once its parts are named.
senses.whyCN: 城市被分成有名字的几块，才读得懂。

senses.title: An area marked for a purpose
senses.definition: an area of a country set apart for a particular use or rule
senses.definitionCN: 为一个用途或一套规则划出的一片地方
senses.example: The mining district employs thousands.
senses.exampleCN: 矿区雇了成千上万人。
senses.why: A border on a map is a decision before it is a place.
senses.whyCN: 地图上的界线，先是一个决定，然后才是一个地方。

intro.en: District comes from Latin districtus, a territory under a lord, from distringere, to draw tight.
intro.cn: district 来自拉丁语 districtus（辖地），源头是 distringere（拉紧、约束）。

items.en: Stringere meant to draw tight or bind.
items.cn: stringere 指拉紧或捆住。

items.en: Distringere added the sense of holding under control.
items.cn: distringere 添上管住、约束的意思。

items.en: Districtus named the land held under one authority.
items.cn: districtus 指归一个权力管辖的土地。

items.en: Old French districte kept the legal flavour.
items.cn: 古法语 districte 保留了法律意味。

items.en: English widened it to any marked part of a place.
items.cn: 英语后来把它扩大到任何划出的一片地方。

items.en: A school, a shop and a mine can each have a district.
items.cn: 今天学校、商店与矿山都可以有自己的区。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the strict stem, while the meaning group lists other names for a piece of land.
note.cn: 形近组共享 strict 这段词干，近义组则是几种表示一片地方的说法。

entries.definition: firm and not allowing exceptions
entries.definitionCN: 严格而不许例外

entries.definition: to keep within limits
entries.definitionCN: 限制在范围内

entries.definition: a rule that limits something
entries.definitionCN: 限制性的规定

entries.definition: a part of a place with no clear edge
entries.definitionCN: 一片边界不明确的地方

entries.definition: a large part of a country
entries.definitionCN: 国家里的一大片

entries.definition: an area marked off for one use
entries.definitionCN: 为某种用途划出的地带

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a pencil line around four streets and end with a mine that has its own name.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从围着四条街的铅笔线开始，落到一座有自己的名字的矿。

normal.en: Dis- plus strict: a line is drawn tight around a piece of land.
normal.cn: dis 加 strict，一根线把一片地紧紧圈住。

normal.en: The market district is loud until midnight.
normal.cn: 市场区一直吵到半夜。

normal.en: Every district sends one teacher to the meeting.
normal.cn: 每个区派一名老师来开会。

normal.en: The school district redrew its borders last year.
normal.cn: 学区去年重画了边界。

normal.en: Coal built this district and then left it quiet.
normal.cn: 煤把这个区建起来，然后让它安静下来。

abstract.en: Picture a pencil square drawn around four streets.
abstract.cn: 想象用铅笔围着四条街画一个方块。

abstract.en: Picture a gate with a name board above it.
abstract.cn: 想象一道门，门楣上挂着一块名牌。

abstract.en: Picture a map cut into pieces by thin lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图被细线切成几块。

examples.en: The old district is full of small bookshops.
examples.cn: 老城区到处都是小书店。

examples.en: She works in the business district near the station.
examples.cn: 她在车站附近的商业区上班。

examples.en: Each district has its own fire station.
examples.cn: 每个区都有自己的消防站。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 district 记成「圈起来的一片」：dis 表示分开，strict 表示拉紧，用线把一片地紧紧圈出，就成了一个区。

root: 源自拉丁语 districtus，来自 distringere（拉紧、约束），本义是被一个权力圈住、受其管辖的一片土地。后来法律意味变淡，只指在地图上划出的一片地方，可用于城区、学区、矿区等。

sensesIntro.en: From a line drawn tight around four streets to a whole region with its own name board.
sensesIntro.cn: 从绕着四条街紧紧画出的一根线，到一整片挂着自己名牌的地区。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small square on an old town map, outlined in pencil along four streets.
core.cn: 核心意象：老城地图上用铅笔沿四条街描出的一小块。

chain: A NAME IS PUT ON IT

branches.en: The first sense is a named part of a town.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是城市里有名字的一片。

branches.en: The second sense is land marked off for a use.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是为某种用途划出的地。

branches.en: Both senses are made by a line someone decided on.
branches.cn: 两个义项都靠某人决定的一条线成立。

branches.en: Both give the people inside a shared name.
branches.cn: 两个义项都给里面的人一个共同的名字。

branches.en: Only the second sense suggests a single industry or rule.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项暗示单一的行业或规则。

intro.en: District belongs to the strict family, where Latin stringere, to draw tight, also gives strict and restrict.
intro.cn: district 属于 strict 一族，拉丁语 stringere（拉紧）也给出 strict 与 restrict。

latinIntro.en: Latin stringere, to draw tight, gives strict; dis- encloses a piece of land under one authority.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stringere（拉紧）给出 strict，前缀 dis- 把一片地圈在一个权力之下。

items.meaning: land drawn tight under one rule
items.example: The district has its own council.
A restriction on water use began.

items.meaning: in a firm and exact way

definition_zh: 工作室；演播室；单间公寓
definition_en: a room where an artist works, a place where films or programmes are made, or a small flat with one main room
core_image: 一间大窗明亮的房间，画架、灯光和工具各就各位
scene: 画家在她的工作室里作画。 The painter works in her studio.
sceneCN: 这里 studio 是「工作室」（第 1 个义项）；句意：画家在她的工作室里作画。

senses.title: An artist's room
senses.definition: a room where an artist or photographer works
senses.definitionCN: 艺术家或摄影师工作的房间
senses.example: The painter works in her studio.
senses.exampleCN: 画家在她的工作室里作画。
senses.why: This is a room made for making.
senses.whyCN: 这是一个为创作而设的房间。

senses.title: A production room
senses.definition: a place where films, music, or programmes are recorded
senses.definitionCN: 录制电影、音乐或节目的场所
senses.example: The band recorded the song in a studio.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队在录音棚里录了这首歌。
senses.why: Cameras and microphones need a controlled room.
senses.whyCN: 摄像机和麦克风需要一个可控的房间。

senses.title: A small flat
senses.definition: a small flat with one main room
senses.definitionCN: 只有一个主要房间的小公寓
senses.example: She rents a studio near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 她在车站附近租了一间单间公寓。
senses.why: One room serves for living and working.
senses.whyCN: 一个房间兼作起居与工作。

intro.en: Studio comes from Italian studio, a room for study or art.
intro.cn: studio 来自意大利语 studio，意为学习或创作之室。

items.en: Studium meant eager study.
items.cn: studium 意为热切的钻研。

items.en: Studio named a study or workroom.
items.cn: studio 指书房或工作室。

items.en: Studio named an artist's workroom.
items.cn: studio 指艺术家的工作室。

items.en: It moved into film and music production.
items.cn: 它进入电影与音乐制作领域。

items.en: It also named a one-room flat.
items.cn: 它也指只有一个房间的公寓。

entries.definition: a person who studies

entries.definition: things in general
entries.definitionCN: 东西

entries.definitionCN: 画室

entries.definition: a room for showing art

normalIntro.en: Studio is a room where making happens, from paint to film to living.
normalIntro.cn: studio 是让创作发生的房间，从颜料到电影，再到生活。

normal.en: The artist cleaned her studio.
normal.cn: 画家打扫了她的画室。

normal.en: They built a new film studio.
normal.cn: 他们建了新的电影制片厂。

normal.en: The song was recorded in a studio.
normal.cn: 这首歌在录音棚录制。

normal.en: The TV studio was full of lights.

abstract.en: A studio is a room that listens to its worker.
abstract.cn: 工作室，是一间听工作者话的房间。

abstract.en: One room can hold both a bed and a beginning.
abstract.cn: 一个房间，能同时装下床和起点。

abstract.en: Every finished work leaves a studio behind.
abstract.cn: 每件完成的作品背后，都有一间工作室。

examples.en: The painter works in her studio.
examples.cn: 画家在她的工作室里作画。

examples.en: The band recorded the song in a studio.
examples.cn: 乐队在录音棚里录了这首歌。

examples.en: She rents a studio near the station.
examples.cn: 她在车站附近租了一间单间公寓。

dict_mnemonic.text: studio 原指「钻研之室」；画家在里面作画是工作室，乐队在里面录音是录音棚，一个人住在里面就是单间公寓。

root: 来自意大利语 studio（书房、工作室），源于拉丁语 studium（钻研）；由艺术家的创作房间，扩展到影视与音乐制作场所，再指一室一厅的小公寓。

sensesIntro.en: Studio is an artist's room, a recording room, or a one-room home.
sensesIntro.cn: studio 是艺术家的房间、录制节目的房间，或只有一个房间的家。

core.en: A bright room with tools laid out.
core.cn: 一间摆好工具、光线明亮的房间。

branches.en: A brush rests beside a canvas.
branches.cn: 画笔放在画布旁。

branches.en: A microphone hangs from the ceiling.
branches.cn: 麦克风吊在天花板上。

branches.en: A bed and a desk share one room.
branches.cn: 床和书桌共用一个房间。

branches.en: Both art and sound need a controlled room.
branches.cn: 艺术与声音都需要一个可控的房间。

branches.en: A small studio can still hold big work.
branches.cn: 小小的工作室，也能装下大作品。

intro.en: Studio forms a plural and compounds for flats.
intro.cn: studio 有复数形式，并能构成公寓相关复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is studium, through Italian studio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语来源是 studium，经意大利语 studio 进入英语。

definition_zh: 费用；会费；酬金
definition_en: money paid for a service, for membership or study, or as a reward for professional work
core_image: 报名表最后一栏印着金额，旁边有人正低头数着零钱
scene: 报名表最后一栏写着参加活动的价格。 The entrance fee is ten dollars.
sceneCN: 这里 fee 是「费用」（第 1 个义项）；句意：入场费是十美元。

senses.title: A payment for a service
senses.definition: money charged for a service or for permission to do something
senses.definitionCN: 为服务或获准做某事而收取的钱
senses.example: There is a small fee for the service.
senses.exampleCN: 这项服务收取少量费用。
senses.why: This is the broad modern sense of a charge.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示收费的宽泛现代义。

senses.title: A membership or study charge
senses.definition: money paid regularly to belong to a group or to study
senses.definitionCN: 为加入团体或学习而定期支付的钱
senses.example: She paid the membership fee online.
senses.exampleCN: 她在网上支付了会费。
senses.why: Regular charges for groups and schools use the same word.
senses.whyCN: 团体与学校的定期收费也用同一个词。

senses.title: A professional reward
senses.definition: money paid to a professional for their work
senses.definitionCN: 支付给专业人士的工作报酬
senses.example: The lawyer charged a high fee.
senses.exampleCN: 律师收取了高额费用。
senses.why: The sense moves from access charges to payment for skill.
senses.whyCN: 该义从准入收费转向对专业技能的报酬。

intro.en: Fee goes back to Old English feoh, which meant cattle and then money.
intro.cn: fee 可追溯到古英语 feoh，本义是牲畜，后来指钱财。

items.en: The root named cattle and movable wealth.
items.cn: 该词根表示牲畜与可移动的财富。

items.en: Feoh meant cattle, goods, or money.
items.cn: feoh 意为牲畜、财产或钱财。

items.en: Fee came to mean a payment or reward.
items.cn: fee 开始表示支付的款项或报酬。

items.en: The word narrowed to charges for services and rights.
items.cn: 该词缩小为服务与权利的收费。

items.en: Fee now covers tuition, membership, and professional charges.
items.cn: 现代英语中 fee 涵盖学费、会费与专业收费。

note.en: Fee is compared with similar-looking words and with words for payments.
note.cn: 把 fee 与形近词以及表示付款的词作比较。

entries.definition: a flying insect that makes honey
entries.definitionCN: 蜜蜂

entries.definition: the plural of foot
entries.definitionCN: 脚（复数）

entries.definition: weak and without energy
entries.definitionCN: 虚弱的

entries.definition: an amount asked for a service
entries.definitionCN: 收费

entries.definition: money given for something
entries.definitionCN: 付款

entries.definition: the amount needed to buy something
entries.definitionCN: 费用；成本

normalIntro.en: A fee is the money charged for a service, a membership, or professional work.
normalIntro.cn: fee 是为服务、会籍或专业工作收取的钱。

normal.en: Fee and free differ by one letter.
normal.cn: fee 与 free 只差一个字母。

normal.en: Tuition fees are payments for study.
normal.cn: tuition fees 是学费。

normal.en: An entrance fee lets you go in.
normal.cn: entrance fee 是让你进入场所的费用。

normal.en: Lawyers and doctors charge fees for their work.
normal.cn: 律师和医生为工作收取酬金。

normal.en: Fee came from an old word for cattle.
normal.cn: fee 源自一个表示牲畜的古老词。

abstract.en: Wealth first walked on four legs, then became money.
abstract.cn: 财富最初长着四条腿，后来变成了钱。

abstract.en: A fee marks the border between free and paid.
abstract.cn: 费用标出免费与付费之间的界线。

abstract.en: Small fees can add up to a large burden.
abstract.cn: 小额费用也可能累积成沉重负担。

examples.en: There is a small fee for the service.
examples.cn: 这项服务收取少量费用。

examples.en: She paid the membership fee online.
examples.cn: 她在网上支付了会费。

examples.en: The lawyer charged a high fee.
examples.cn: 律师收取了高额费用。

dict_mnemonic.text: fee 源自古英语 feoh（牲畜、钱财），古人以牲畜计财富，词义后来固定为「费用、酬金」。

root: 源自古英语 feoh（牲畜、钱财），出自日耳曼语词根，核心义「为服务或权利付出的钱」。

sensesIntro.en: Fee means money charged for a service, paid for membership or study, or given as professional pay.
sensesIntro.cn: fee 意为服务收费、会费或学费，以及支付给专业人士的酬金。

core.en: Money exchanged for access, membership, or skilled work.
core.cn: 为准入、会籍或专业工作而支付的金钱。

branches.en: A charge for a service.
branches.cn: 服务收费。

branches.en: A regular charge for belonging or studying.
branches.cn: 加入团体或学习的定期收费。

branches.en: Payment for professional work.
branches.cn: 专业工作的报酬。

branches.en: Access and membership are both bought with fees.

branches.en: A service charge and a professional reward can be the same sum.
branches.cn: 服务费与专业报酬可能是同一笔钱。

intro.en: Fee forms a small family for charges, payers, and old land law.
intro.cn: fee 构成表示收费、缴费者与古代土地法的少量词族。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, so Latin entries are not its direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属日耳曼语，拉丁条目并非其直接来源。

每位缴费者都会收到收据。

items.meaning: a worker who brings in fees

items.example: The land is held in fee simple.

items.meaning: land passed only to direct heirs

definition_zh: 物种；种类；（法律）形式；类型
definition_en: a group of living things that share characteristics and can breed with each other, or a kind or type of something
core_image: 一张按属种排好的标本柜，每个抽屉装着一类能互相繁育的生命
scene: 博物馆的标本柜排成长长一列，讲解员轻轻拉开一只抽屉。 This drawer holds a bird species found only on that remote island.
sceneCN: 这里 species 是「物种」（第 1 个义项：能互相繁育的一类生物）；句意为这个抽屉装着只在那座偏远岛屿上发现的鸟类物种。图中可辨识物件：标本柜、抽屉、鸟类标本。

collocations.zh: 侵入某个物种的栖息地

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「物种形成；物种分化」
与本词同源于拉丁 specere「观看」，义为「标本；样本」
由 sub- 加本词构成，义为「亚种」

senses.title: A group of breeding organisms
senses.titleCN: 物种：能互相繁育的一类生物
senses.definition: a group of living organisms that resemble one another and can interbreed to produce fertile young
senses.definitionCN: 彼此相似、能互相交配繁殖出可育后代的一类生物
senses.example: This frog species exists only in the mountain streams of the island.
senses.exampleCN: 这种青蛙只存在于那座岛的山间溪流中。
senses.why: Latin species meant an appearance or a kind; biologists fixed the word to the natural kind that keeps breeding true.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 species 本指「外貌、种类」；生物学家把这个固定在能稳定繁衍后代的那一类自然生命上。

senses.title: A kind or type of thing
senses.definition: a kind, sort, or variety of something, especially when it is one among many
senses.definitionCN: 某物的种类、类别或样式，尤指众多之中的一类
senses.example: The shop sells many species of cactus from dry deserts.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店售卖许多来自干旱沙漠的仙人掌种类。
senses.why: The classifying image extends beyond life: anything that can be sorted into a kind can be called a species.
senses.whyCN: 分类的意象延伸到生命之外：凡能归入一类的都可称一种 species。

senses.title: Human beings as a kind
senses.definition: the human species, considered as one biological kind among others
senses.definitionCN: 把人类当作生物中的一种来看待
senses.example: The human species has changed the climate of the whole planet.
senses.exampleCN: 人类这一物种改变了整个星球的气候。
senses.why: People themselves form one of the kinds in the great cabinet of living things.
senses.whyCN: 人类本身就是生命大柜中的一格。

senses.title: The outward appearance or form
senses.definition: the visible form or appearance of something, especially in legal or philosophical language
senses.definitionCN: 事物的外在形式或样貌，多见于法律或哲学术语
senses.example: In old legal texts, species referred to the exact form of the property.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧法律文本中，species 指财产的确切形式。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, close to the Latin root: what shows itself to the eye.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，贴近拉丁词根：呈现在眼前的样子。

senses.title: In chemistry: a distinct form
senses.titleCN: 化学物种：一种确定的形态
senses.definition: a distinct kind of atom, molecule, or ion present in a substance or reaction
senses.definitionCN: 物质或反应中存在的某种确定的原子、分子或离子形态
senses.example: The reaction produces several charged species in the solution.
senses.exampleCN: 该反应在溶液中产生几种带电的化学物种。
senses.why: Chemistry borrowed the sorting image: each distinct molecular kind is a species of its own.
senses.whyCN: 化学借用了分类意象：每种确定的分子形态自成一个 species。

senses.title: A specific variety within a genus
senses.definition: the taxonomic rank below genus in the classification of living things
senses.definitionCN: 生物分类中低于「属」的一个层级
senses.example: The genus roses contains over one hundred species.
senses.exampleCN: 蔷薇属包含一百多个物种。
senses.why: In the ladder of classification, species is the rung directly under genus.
senses.whyCN: 在分类的阶梯上，物种是紧挨「属」下面的一级。

senses.title: Companion species: coexistence
senses.definition: a species that lives alongside another and depends on or affects it
senses.definitionCN: 与另一物种共同生活、依赖或影响它的物种
senses.example: Ants are companion species for many flowering plants.
senses.exampleCN: 蚂蚁是许多开花植物的伴生物种。
senses.why: Kinds do not live alone: each kind is defined partly by the company it keeps.
senses.whyCN: 物种不是孤立生活的：每个物种的定义部分取决于它所相伴的对象。

senses.title: Endangered species as a category
senses.titleCN: 濒危物种：受威胁的一类
senses.definition: a species whose numbers have fallen so far that it may disappear
senses.definitionCN: 数量已下降到可能消失程度的一类生物
senses.example: The panda was long listed as an endangered species.
senses.exampleCN: 大熊猫长期被列为濒危物种。
senses.why: The cabinet drawer can close forever: a kind that dies out is a kind lost.
senses.whyCN: 柜子的抽屉可能永远合上：灭绝的一类就是永远失去的一类。

intro.en: Species comes from Latin through frequent philosophical and scientific use, and its whole story is about seeing and sorting.
intro.cn: species 来自拉丁语，经过哲学与科学的长期使用，整个故事围绕「观看与分类」展开。

items.en: *spek- is generally reconstructed as "to observe, look at". The deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *spek- 表示「观察、看」；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: In Latin, species meant "appearance, form, a particular kind", from specere "to look at".
items.cn: 拉丁语 species 由 specere「看」派生，意为「外貌、形式、特定的种类」。

items.en: Medieval philosophers used species for the form things impress on the mind, alongside genus.
items.cn: 中世纪哲学家把 species 用于事物印入心灵的形式，与 genus「属」并立。

items.en: The word entered English in the sixteenth century with the senses of kind and outward form.
items.cn: 该词于十六世纪进入英语，带有「种类」与「外在形式」两义。

items.en: Biologists from Ray to Darwin made species the basic unit of classification and evolution.
items.cn: 从雷到达尔文，生物学家把物种确立为分类与进化的基本单位。

items.en: Everyday English uses species both for living kinds and loosely for any sort of thing.
items.cn: 现代英语既用它指生物物种，也泛指任何一类东西。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same seeing root and similar spellings; the near-meaning group gathers words for kinds and sorts.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「观看」词根的词与拼写相近的词；近义组收表示种类、类别的词。

entries.definition: A single example taken from a group for study; from the same Latin root specere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「标本、样本」，从同一拉丁词根 specere 派生。

entries.definition: A technical verb meaning to form new species in evolution.
entries.definitionCN: 专业动词，义为「形成新物种」。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning particular or distinctive; from the same family of Latin words.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「特别的、专门的」，来自同一拉丁词族。

entries.definition: Something striking to look at; built on the same seeing root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「景象、奇观」，建立在同一「观看」词根上。

entries.definition: Plural of spice, the kitchen ingredient; merely looks similar and is of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: spice 的复数，指香料；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A general word for a class of similar things; everyday and not biological.
entries.definitionCN: 表示一类相似之物的常用词，日常用语，不带生物学色彩。

entries.definition: The taxonomic rank above species; it groups several species together.
entries.definitionCN: 分类学中高于种的层级，把若干物种归为一组。

entries.definition: A subdivision within a species, or simply a diverse assortment.
entries.definitionCN: 物种内部的细分单元，或泛指多样的种类。

entries.definition: A cultivated variety within an animal species, especially domestic ones.
entries.definitionCN: 动物物种内部培育出的品种，尤指家养动物。

entries.definition: A general class in any system of sorting, not tied to living things.
entries.definitionCN: 任何分类体系中的大类，不限于生物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根，以及该词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: specere is to look: a species is a kind you can point to once you have looked.
normal.cn: specere 意为「看」：物种就是看过之后能明确指出的一类。

normal.en: The same root gives inspect, spectator and respect; all involve looking.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 inspect、spectator、respect，都与「看」有关。

normal.en: An endangered species is a kind on the edge of vanishing.
normal.cn: endangered species 指濒临消失的物种。

normal.en: Biologists define a species by breeding: members can produce fertile young.
normal.cn: 生物学家以繁育定义物种：同种成员能繁殖可育后代。

normal.en: The phrase origin of species names the famous book by Darwin.
normal.cn: origin of species 是达尔文名著《物种起源》的书名。

abstract.en: Picture a long cabinet of drawers: each drawer holds one kind of life, neatly labelled.
abstract.cn: 想象一排抽屉柜：每个抽屉装着一类生命，标签整齐。

abstract.en: Two animals belong in the same drawer when their young can also breed.
abstract.cn: 当两种动物的后代也能繁育时，它们属于同一个抽屉。

abstract.en: A closed drawer forever is an extinct kind: the label remains, the life is gone.
abstract.cn: 永远合上的抽屉就是灭绝的一类：标签还在，生命已逝。

examples.en: Scientists discovered a new species of owl in the rainforest.
examples.cn: 科学家在雨林中发现了一个新的猫头鹰物种。

examples.en: The wetland shelters dozens of bird species every winter.
examples.cn: 这片湿地每年冬天庇护数十种鸟类。

examples.en: Human activity threatens thousands of species with extinction.
examples.cn: 人类活动威胁着数以千计的物种，使其面临灭绝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯比西兹」——柜子里的标本彼此相似：一类物种

root: 拉丁语 species「外貌、种类」由动词 specere「观看」派生；一般认为原始印欧语 *spek- 表示「观察」，更早来源不确定。同一词根生出 spectare「注视」与希腊语 skopein「看」。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of species move from the biological kind outward: sorting any things into kinds, humans as one kind among them, and the fixed ranks of classification.
sensesIntro.cn: species 的义项从生物学物种向外扩展：把万物归为类别、把人类视为其中一类，再到分类学固定层级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a labelled cabinet where each drawer holds one kind of living thing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排贴着标签的柜子，每个抽屉装着一类生物。

branches.en: THE BIOLOGY LINE: the kind that breeds true sits at a fixed rung below genus.
branches.cn: 生物学线：能稳定繁育的一类位于「属」下面的固定层级。

branches.en: THE SORTING LINE: any things that resemble each other can be called a kind, humans included.
branches.cn: 归类线：彼此相似的任何事物都可称为一类，人类也在其中。

branches.en: THE OLD FORM LINE: before biology, the word meant the outward appearance itself.
branches.cn: 古义线：在生物学之前，这个词指外在形式本身。

branches.en: THE CHEMISTRY LINE: each distinct molecular form becomes its own kind.
branches.cn: 化学线：每种确定的分子形态自成一 kind。

branches.en: THE LIVING-TOGETHER LINE: kinds coexist with others, and some now stand at the edge of vanishing.
branches.cn: 共存线：物种与其他物种相伴而生，有些如今濒临消失。

intro.en: Species is a bare Latin noun; English builds on it mostly through the related seeing root.
intro.cn: species 本身是拉丁名词；英语主要通过相关的「观看」词根在其上构词。

latinIntro.en: Latin specere and its derivatives are well recorded; only the Indo-European root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 specere 及其派生词均有文献记录，只有印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.example: The root appears in spectator and inspect.
items.exampleCN: 该词根出现在 spectator 与 inspect 中。

items.example: The verb is the parent of species.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 species 的来源。

items.example: The noun names what is seen as a kind.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指被看作一类的东西。
它构成 specimen 与 speciation。

items.example: It appears in spectacle and inspect.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 spectacle 与 inspect 中。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「物种形成；物种分化」
与本词同源于拉丁 specere「观看」，义为「标本；样本」
由 sub- 加本词构成，义为「亚种」

definition_zh: 大约的；近似的；接近；近似；估算
definition_en: close to a particular number or state but not exact; to come close to a value, or to estimate something roughly
core_image: 两支箭落在靶心附近，却没有一支正中
scene: 地图铺在桌上，铅笔在两点之间画了一条线。 The distance is approximate because the road curves.
sceneCN: 这里 approximate 是「大约的；近似的」（第 1 个义项：接近某一数值但不精确）；句意为「这个距离只是近似的，因为道路是弯的」。画面里有摊开的地图、两点之间的铅笔线与一把量尺。

pos.zh: 形容词：大约的；近似的；大致相似的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「大约；近似地」
由本词加 -ation 构成，义为「近似值；近似」
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「近似的」
由同一拉丁词根 proximus 派生，义为「邻近；接近」

senses.title: Close but not exact
senses.definition: close to a particular number, amount, or description but not exactly correct
senses.definitionCN: 接近某个数值、数量或描述，但不完全精确
senses.example: The distance is approximate because the road curves.
senses.exampleCN: 这个距离只是近似的，因为道路是弯的。
senses.why: Late Latin approximare meant to come very near; the adjective describes what stands near the true value without touching it.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁语 approximare 意为靠得很近；形容词描述的是贴近真值却没有碰上的东西。

senses.title: To come close to a value
senses.definition: to come close to a particular value, standard, or quality
senses.definitionCN: 接近某个数值、标准或品质
senses.example: His account approximates the truth without being exact.
senses.exampleCN: 他的叙述接近真相，但并不完全准确。
senses.why: The verb keeps the movement: getting nearer to a target.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了那个动作：向目标靠近。

senses.title: To estimate roughly
senses.definition: to calculate or estimate something roughly rather than exactly
senses.definitionCN: 对某物作粗略而非精确的计算或估计
senses.example: We approximated the cost at two thousand pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 我们估算费用约为两千英镑。
senses.why: An estimate is a number placed near the true figure, as near as one can get.
senses.whyCN: 估算是把一个数字放在真值附近，能靠多近就靠多近。

senses.title: To resemble closely
senses.definition: to resemble something closely in appearance or character
senses.definitionCN: 在外观或特征上与被比较之物很接近
senses.example: The copy approximates the original very well.
senses.exampleCN: 这件仿品与原件非常接近。
senses.why: Two things can stand near each other without being the same.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西可以彼此靠得很近，却并不相同。

intro.en: Approximate is built on the Latin word for nearest, and it names what stands close to the truth.
intro.cn: approximate 建立在拉丁语「最近的」一词上，命名的是贴近真相的东西。

items.en: Prope 'near' is the adverb behind the whole family of closeness.
items.cn: prope「近」是整族表示接近的词背后的副词。

items.en: Proximus is the superlative, 'nearest', and it also gives English proximity.
items.cn: proximus 是最高级「最近的」，它还生出英语的 proximity。

items.en: Ad- plus proximus formed approximare, 'to come near to'.
items.cn: ad- 与 proximus 构成 approximare，意为「靠近」。

items.en: The adjective and verb appear in English in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries.
items.cn: 形容词与动词在十五、十六世纪先后出现在英语里。

items.en: The word covers rough figures, close copies and near matches of every kind.
items.cn: 这个词覆盖粗略数字、接近的仿品与各种近似匹配。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the proximity family; the near-meaning group gathers words for rough and close.
note.cn: 形近组收表示「邻近」的词族；近义组收表示粗略与接近的词。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning roughly or about.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词派生的副词，义为「大约、近似地」。

entries.definition: A result or description that is close but not exact.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「近似值、近似」，是本词的抽象名词。

entries.definition: Nearest in space, time, or cause.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最接近的、直接的」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: The state of being near.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「邻近、接近」。

entries.definition: Not exact, made without careful measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「粗略的」，与 approximate 的估算义接近。

entries.definition: Calculated by judgement rather than measured exactly.
entries.definitionCN: 靠判断而非精确测量得出的，对应 approximate 的估计义。

entries.definition: Near in space, value, or similarity.
entries.definitionCN: 空间、数值或相似度上接近，对应 approximate 的核心义。

entries.definition: Used before a number to mean roughly.
entries.definitionCN: 用在数字前表示「大约」，是最口语的近似说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use proximus, the Latin word for nearest, and the picture of an arrow near the bullseye.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子用拉丁语 proximus「最近的」，以及箭落在靶心附近的画面。

normal.en: Proximus means nearest; approximate means near the exact value.
normal.cn: proximus 意为最近的；approximate 就是靠近精确值。

normal.en: An arrow beside the bullseye is an approximate hit.
normal.cn: 落在靶心旁边的箭，就是近似的一击。

normal.en: A rough estimate is a number placed near the truth.
normal.cn: 粗略的估算，是把数字放在真相附近。

normal.en: A good copy stands close to the original.
normal.cn: 好的仿品站得离原件很近。

normal.en: Approximately is the adverb you use before a rough figure.
normal.cn: approximately 就是放在粗略数字前的副词。

abstract.en: The word lives in the gap between the exact and the near.
abstract.cn: 这个词住在「精确」与「接近」之间的缝隙里。

abstract.en: It lets thought work with numbers it cannot fully know.
abstract.cn: 它让思维可以使用自己无法完全知晓的数字。

abstract.en: Almost right is its whole territory.
abstract.cn: 「几乎对」就是它的全部领地。

examples.en: The distance is approximate because the road curves.
examples.cn: 这个距离只是近似的，因为道路是弯的。

examples.en: We approximated the cost at two thousand pounds.
examples.cn: 我们估算费用约为两千英镑。

examples.en: The copy approximates the original very well.
examples.cn: 这件仿品与原件非常接近。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普罗克西梅特」——箭落在靶心旁边，差一点点：大约的；近似

root: approximate 来自晚期拉丁语 approximare「靠近」，该动词由 ad- 与 proximus「最近的」构成，proximus 又是 prope「近」的最高级。这个词的核心始终是「贴近而未必正中」：一个数字贴近真值就是近似值，一份叙述贴近真相就是接近，一笔费用靠估算贴近实际就是估算，一件仿品贴近原件就是大致相似。

sensesIntro.en: Four uses all stand near a target without hitting it: a rough figure, a close account, an estimate, and a good copy.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个用法都站在目标附近而没有正中：粗略的数字、接近的叙述、估算，以及逼真的仿品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow stuck just beside the bullseye.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支箭扎在靶心旁边。

branches.en: THE VALUE LINE: the number stands near the true one.
branches.cn: 数值线：这个数字站在真值附近。

branches.en: THE MOVEMENT LINE: the verb moves toward a target.
branches.cn: 动作线：动词向目标移动。

branches.en: THE ESTIMATE LINE: a rough figure is placed near the truth.
branches.cn: 估算线：粗略的数字被放在真相附近。

branches.en: THE COPY LINE: a likeness stands close to its original.
branches.cn: 仿品线：相似之物站在原件附近。

branches.en: THE MEASURE LINE: both adjective and estimate accept a small gap.
branches.cn: 度量线：形容词与估算都容许一点差距。

intro.en: Approximate is a Latin verb and adjective built on proximus, and its family is easy to read.
intro.cn: approximate 是建立在 proximus 上的拉丁动词与形容词，词族很容易辨认。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is real: proximus 'nearest' is the source of the whole group.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是真实的：proximus「最近的」是整组词的源头。

items.example: The trip takes approximately two hours.
items.exampleCN: 这段行程大约需要两小时。

items.example: The model is only an approximation.
items.exampleCN: 这个模型只是一个近似。

items.meaning: of the nature of a near match
items.example: The term has an approximative sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个说法带有近似的意味。

items.example: The proximate cause was a loose wire.
The proximity of the sea cooled the air.
items.exampleCN: 海水的邻近让空气变凉。

items.example: The result approximates to the predicted value.
The builder gave an approximate estimate.
items.exampleCN: 施工者给了一个粗略的估算。

definition_zh: 分析；分解；化验；解析；进行精神分析
definition_en: to examine something by breaking it into its parts, especially to understand its structure, composition or meaning
core_image: 把一团缠结的线慢慢拆开，露出一根根单独的线头
scene: 实验室的灯亮到深夜，桌上一排试管贴着标签，记录本摊开着。 The team analysed the water from six wells before making any recommendation.
sceneCN: 这里 analysed 是「分析化验」（第 1 个义项：把整体拆开来研究）；句意为小组在提出任何建议之前，先分析了六口井的水。画面里有深夜的实验室、贴标签的试管与摊开的记录本。

pos.zh: 动词：分析；分解；化验；解析；进行精神分析

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语名词 analysis 借入，义为「分析；分析结果」，与动词同源
由 analysis 加 -ist 构成，义为「分析师；化验员」
由希腊语 analytikos 借入，义为「分析的；解析的」
由 analytic 加 -al 构成，义为「善于分析的；分析性的」
由 analytical 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「以分析的方式」

senses.title: To break a whole into parts
senses.definition: to examine something complex by separating it into its parts and studying how they fit together
senses.definitionCN: 把复杂事物拆成各个部分，研究它们如何组合，从而弄清整体
senses.example: Researchers analysed the survey data for three months.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员花了三个月分析调查数据。
senses.why: Greek analyein is to loosen up: the whole is untied into its parts so that each can be seen.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 analyein 是「松开」：把整体解开成各个部分，好让每一部分都看得见。

senses.title: To test the composition of a substance
senses.definition: to test a substance in a laboratory to find out what it contains
senses.definitionCN: 在实验室检验某物质，查明其中含有什么成分
senses.example: The lab analysed the soil for traces of lead.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室分析了土壤，查找铅的痕迹。
senses.why: Chemical analysis separates a substance into its elements, which is the loosening image made literal.
senses.whyCN: 化学分析把物质分离成元素，正是「拆开」这个意象的字面实现。

senses.title: To parse a sentence
senses.definition: to describe the grammatical structure of a sentence by identifying its parts
senses.definitionCN: 识别句子的各个成分，说明其语法结构
senses.example: Students analysed the sentence clause by clause.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们一个从句一个从句地解析这个句子。
senses.why: Grammar treats a sentence as a built object, and analysis takes it apart to show the joints.
senses.whyCN: 语法把句子当作一个搭建起来的物件，分析就是把它拆开，露出接缝。

senses.title: To practise psychoanalysis
senses.definition: to treat a patient by exploring unconscious thoughts and feelings over a series of sessions
senses.definitionCN: 通过一系列会谈探究病人的潜意识想法与情感，以此治疗
senses.example: The therapist analysed the patient's dreams over several sessions.
senses.exampleCN: 治疗师在几次会谈中分析了病人的梦。
senses.why: The mind is treated as a layered structure, and therapy loosens the layers to reach what lies underneath.
senses.whyCN: 心灵被当作有层次的结构，治疗就是把层层结构松开，抵达藏在下面的东西。

senses.title: To assess a situation or market
senses.definition: to study a situation, market or strategy systematically in order to judge it or plan action
senses.definitionCN: 系统地研究局势、市场或策略，以便作出判断或制定行动
senses.example: Analysts analysed the market carefully before the merger was announced.
senses.exampleCN: 合并宣布之前，分析师们仔细分析了市场。
senses.why: A market is a complex whole of prices, buyers and risks; breaking it into factors is how a decision is prepared.
senses.whyCN: 市场是价格、买家与风险构成的复杂整体；把它拆成若干因素，正是为决策做准备。

intro.en: Analyse is a Greek verb of loosening that came to English through Latin and French, and its spelling still divides the Atlantic.
intro.cn: analyse 是一个表示「松开」的希腊动词，经拉丁语与法语进入英语，它的拼写至今仍横跨大西洋两岸。

items.en: The verb lyein meant 'to loosen, release, untie'. It is the root of a large family of Greek words.
items.cn: 动词 lyein 意为「松开、释放、解开」，是希腊语一大族词的词根。

items.en: Ana- 'up, throughout' plus lyein formed analyein, 'to loosen up, undo, resolve into elements'.
items.cn: 前缀 ana-「向上、彻底」与 lyein 构成 analyein，意为「松开、拆解、分解成元素」。

items.en: The noun analysis meant 'a dissolving, a resolution', especially of a complex whole into its parts.
items.cn: 名词 analysis 意为「分解、解析」，尤指把复杂整体拆成部分。

items.en: Latin analysis carried the Greek noun into learned use, and the Latin adjective analyticus followed.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 analysis 把这个希腊名词带入学术语言，拉丁形容词 analyticus 也随之出现。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the seventeenth century and formed the verb; early scientific use was close to chemical separation.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入名词并造出动词；早期科学用法接近化学分离。

items.en: British writing keeps analyse and analyser, while American writing uses analyze and analyzer. The pronunciation follows the spelling.
items.cn: 英式写作保留 analyse 与 analyser，美式写作使用 analyze 与 analyzer，读音随拼写而变。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same Greek family and the American spelling; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of close examination.
note.cn: 形近组收同一希腊词族的成员及美式拼写；近义组收表示仔细检查的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the process or result of breaking something into parts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「分析、分析结果」，指拆解整体的过程或结果。

entries.definition: A person who performs analysis, especially of data or finance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「分析师」，指从事分析工作的人，尤指数据或金融领域。

entries.definition: Adjective: relating to analysis or proceeding by separating parts.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「分析的、解析的」，指与拆解研究有关的。

entries.definition: The American spelling and pronunciation of the same verb.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个动词的美式拼写与读音，与 analyse 完全同义。

entries.definition: To look at something closely and carefully, often without taking it apart.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「检查、审视」，强调仔细看，未必拆解。

entries.definition: To judge the value or quality of something after study.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「评估」，指研究之后判断其价值或质量。

entries.definition: To cut something apart in order to study its structure, literally or figuratively.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「解剖、仔细剖析」，字面或比喻上都强调切开来看。

entries.definition: To explain the meaning of something, rather than its structure.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「解释、诠释」，侧重说明含义而不是拆解结构。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Greek loosening root and the spelling split that still marks British and American usage.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的希腊语「松开」词根，以及至今区分英美用法的拼写差异。

normal.en: lyein is to loosen; analysis is the act of loosening a whole into parts.
normal.cn: lyein 是「松开」；analysis 就是把整体松开成部分。

normal.en: ana- means up or throughout, so analyein is to loosen something all the way through.
normal.cn: ana- 表示「向上、彻底」，所以 analyein 是把东西彻底松开。

normal.en: Chemistry made the metaphor literal: analysis separates a substance into its elements.
normal.cn: 化学把这个比喻变成字面：分析把物质分离成元素。

normal.en: The British verb is analyse, the American analyze; both come from the same noun.
normal.cn: 英式动词是 analyse，美式是 analyze，两者都来自同一个名词。

normal.en: Analyst adds -ist to analysis: the person who does the loosening.
normal.cn: analyst 在 analysis 后加 -ist：做「拆解」这件事的人。

abstract.en: Picture a knotted ball of string slowly unwinding until every strand lies separate on the table.
abstract.cn: 想象一团打了结的线慢慢解开，直到每一根都单独躺在桌上。

abstract.en: Picture a watch opened on a cloth, each gear placed in a row so the movement can be understood.
abstract.cn: 想象一只表在布上被打开，每个齿轮排成一行，好让人看懂它怎么走。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence drawn as a diagram, its clauses branching like a tree turned upside down.
abstract.cn: 想象一个句子被画成图解，各从句像一棵倒过来的树那样分叉。

examples.en: The team analysed the water from six wells before making any recommendation.
examples.cn: 小组在提出任何建议之前，先分析了六口井的水。

examples.en: Students analysed the sentence clause by clause.
examples.cn: 学生们一个从句一个从句地解析这个句子。

examples.en: Analysts analysed the market carefully before the merger was announced.
examples.cn: 合并宣布之前，分析师们仔细分析了市场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿拉来撕」——把整团线一根根撕开来看：分析、分解

root: 希腊语动词 lyein「松开」加前缀 ana-「向上、彻底」构成 analyein「拆解」，其名词 analysis「分解」经中世纪拉丁语进入学术语言，再由法语进入英语。英式拼写 analyse，美式拼写 analyze，同源同义。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses apply the same loosening motion to data, to substances, to sentences, to the mind, and to markets.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项把同一个「拆开」的动作分别用到数据、物质、句子、心灵与市场上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a knotted tangle is untied until every separate strand is visible.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团打结的缠结被解开，直到每一根线都看得见。

branches.en: THE STRUCTURE LINE: a complex whole is taken apart to see how it is built.
branches.cn: 结构线：把复杂整体拆开，看清它是怎么搭起来的。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE LINE: chemical testing makes the loosening literal.
branches.cn: 物质线：化学检验把「拆开」变成字面动作。

branches.en: THE SENTENCE LINE: grammar opens a sentence at its joints.
branches.cn: 句子线：语法在句子的接缝处把它打开。

branches.en: THE MIND LINE: therapy loosens the layers of the unconscious.
branches.cn: 心灵线：治疗把潜意识的层次松开。

branches.en: THE DECISION LINE: a market is split into factors so that a judgment can be made.
branches.cn: 决策线：把市场拆成若干因素，以便作出判断。

intro.en: Analyse is built from a Greek prefix, a Greek loosening verb and a noun suffix; English adds its own spelling variants.
intro.cn: analyse 由希腊前缀、表示「松开」的希腊动词与名词后缀构成；英语又加入了自身的拼写变体。

latinIntro.en: The Greek forms are recorded, and Latin analysis and analyticus are documented borrowings from Greek, so no reconstruction is needed here.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语形式有记录，拉丁语 analysis 与 analyticus 也是有文献的希腊借词，因此这里无需重构。

items.example: It intensifies the loosening in analyein.
