items.example: The noun entered English before the verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词先于动词进入英语。

items.meaning: the shared stem of the verb family
items.example: It appears in analyse and analysed.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 analyse 与 analysed 中。

items.example: It forms the British spelling analyse.
It forms the American spelling analyze.

latinEntries.meaning: a dissolving, a resolution into parts

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语 analysis 借入，义为「分析；分析结果」
由 analysis 加 -ist 构成，义为「分析师；化验员」
由 analytic 加 -al 构成，义为「善于分析的」

definition_zh: 慷慨的；大方的；大量的；宽厚的
definition_en: willing to give more than is expected, or larger than usual
core_image: 一个人把满满一篮面包递给邻居
scene: 她给慈善机构捐了一大笔钱，十分慷慨。 She was generous with her donation to the charity.
sceneCN: 这里 generous 是「慷慨的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她给慈善机构捐了一大笔钱，十分慷慨。

senses.title: Free in giving
senses.definition: happy to give money, help, or time
senses.definitionCN: 乐于给予金钱、帮助或时间
senses.example: She was generous with her donation to the charity.
senses.exampleCN: 她给慈善机构捐了一大笔钱，十分慷慨。
senses.why: The old sense of noble birth softened into nobility of giving.
senses.whyCN: 原本「出身高贵」的含义软化为「给予上的高贵」。

senses.title: Larger than usual
senses.definition: larger or more plentiful than is usual or expected
senses.definitionCN: 比通常或预期的更多、更丰盛
senses.example: The cafe serves generous portions of cake.
senses.exampleCN: 这家咖啡馆的蛋糕给得很大份。
senses.why: A generous hand measures out more than the minimum.
senses.whyCN: 慷慨的手总是给出比最低需要更多的东西。

senses.title: Kind in judgment
senses.definition: kind and fair, especially when judging others
senses.definitionCN: 友善公正，尤其在评价他人时
senses.example: He was generous to the new staff.
senses.exampleCN: 他对新员工很宽厚。
senses.why: Giving includes giving others the benefit of the doubt.
senses.whyCN: 给予也包括在存疑时给人留余地。

intro.en: Generous first meant noble by birth and only later meant free in giving.
intro.cn: generous 最初指出身高贵，后来才表示给予慷慨。

items.en: Generosus meant of noble birth.
items.cn: generosus 意为出身高贵的。

items.en: The word passed into French as generous.
items.cn: 这个词以 generous 的形式进入法语。

items.en: English kept the sense of noble character.
items.cn: 英语保留了「品格高贵」的含义。

items.en: Noble character came to mean free in giving.
items.cn: 高贵的品格逐渐引申为乐于给予。

items.en: It also came to describe large amounts.
items.cn: 它也开始形容数量很大。

note.en: Generous is compared with look-alike words and words for giving freely.
note.cn: 把 generous 与形近词以及表示乐于给予的词作比较。

entries.definition: affecting most people or things
entries.definitionCN: 一般的

entries.definition: shared by a whole group
entries.definitionCN: 通用的

entries.definition: very great natural ability
entries.definitionCN: 天才

entries.definition: caring about others
entries.definitionCN: 友善的

entries.definition: giving freely and in large amounts
entries.definitionCN: 大方的

entries.definition: very generous or expensive
entries.definitionCN: 奢华的；极其慷慨的

normalIntro.en: A generous hand gives more than the hand was asked for.
normalIntro.cn: 慷慨的手，给出的总比被要求的更多。

normal.en: She was generous with her donation to the charity.
normal.cn: 她给慈善机构捐了一大笔钱，十分慷慨。

normal.en: The cafe serves generous portions of cake.

normal.en: He was generous to the new staff.

normal.en: They made a generous offer for the house.

normal.en: A generous spirit makes a small gift large.

abstract.en: Generosity is a muscle that grows with use.
abstract.cn: 慷慨是一块越用越强的肌肉。

abstract.en: The hand that opens also learns to receive.
abstract.cn: 张开的手也学会了接受。

abstract.en: What is given freely is never really lost.
abstract.cn: 自由给出的东西从不会真正失去。

dict_mnemonic.text: generous 与 genus（高贵出身）有关：古人认为出身高贵的人品格也高尚，于是「高贵」变成了「慷慨」；generous portion 是「大份」，be generous to 是「对……宽厚」。

root: 来自拉丁语 generosus（出身高贵的），由 genus（族类、出身）引申而来，核心义从「高贵」发展为「慷慨」。

sensesIntro.en: Generous means willing to give freely, larger than usual, or kind in judging others.
sensesIntro.cn: generous 意为乐于给予、比通常更多，或评价他人时宽厚。

core.en: An open hand that gives more than the minimum.
core.cn: 一只给出超过最低需要的手。

branches.en: An open hand passes bread across the table.
branches.cn: 张开的手把面包递过餐桌。

branches.en: The plate is piled higher than anyone asked.
branches.cn: 盘子堆得比谁要求的都高。

branches.en: A judge listens before speaking.
branches.cn: 评判者在开口前先倾听。

branches.en: Giving and forgiving both come from a large heart.
branches.cn: 给予和宽恕都来自一颗宽大的心。

branches.en: Large portions and open hands share one spirit.
branches.cn: 大份的食物与张开的手共享同一种精神。

intro.en: Generous and generosity share the Latin root for noble birth.
intro.cn: generous 与 generosity 共享表示高贵出身的拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin generosus meant of noble birth.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 generosus 意为出身高贵的。

items.example: She is generous with her time.
He generously paid for the meal.

items.exampleCN: 她的慷慨让所有人吃惊。

items.example: The school thanked its donors for their generosities.
items.exampleCN: 学校感谢捐赠者的种种慷慨之举。
那是一个不慷慨的提议。
他的慷慨为他赢得了朋友。

items.example: A generous-hearted neighbour helped us move.
items.exampleCN: 一位心地慷慨的邻居帮我们搬家。

latinEntries.example: Generosus is the source of generous.
latinEntries.exampleCN: generosus 是 generous 的来源。
generositas 孕育了英语的 generosity。

definition_zh: 缘故；理由；为了……起见（for the sake of）
definition_en: used in the phrase for the sake of to mean for the benefit or purpose of someone or something
core_image: 一枚压在决定上的砝码：为了谁、图个什么
scene: 为了孩子们的健康，她把零食都收了起来。 She gave up smoking for the sake of her health.
sceneCN: 这里 sake 是「缘故」（第 1 个义项：for the sake of 表示「为了……的利益」）；句意：为了健康她戒了烟。

collocations.zh: 看在上帝的份上（表示不耐烦）

derivatives.zh: 由 for- 加 sake 构成，义为「抛弃；放弃」，同根近亲
sake 的复数形式，见于 for God's sakes 等感叹用法

senses.title: Benefit or purpose
senses.definition: benefit, advantage, or purpose, used in the phrase for the sake of
senses.definitionCN: 用于 for the sake of 短语，指为了某人的利益或某个目的
senses.example: They moved to the countryside for the sake of the children.
senses.exampleCN: 为了孩子们，他们搬到了乡下。
senses.why: A weight laid on the scale of a decision names the reason that tips it.
senses.whyCN: 压在决定天平上的砝码，正是让决定倾斜的那个「缘故」。

senses.title: In emphatic requests
senses.definition: used in phrases like for God's sake or for heaven's sake to show strong feeling
senses.definitionCN: 用于 for God's sake 等短语，表示强烈情绪或不耐烦
senses.example: For heaven's sake, stop tapping the table!
senses.exampleCN: 看在老天的份上，别再敲桌子了！
senses.why: Calling on the highest witness strengthens a plea like a stamp on a letter.
senses.whyCN: 请出最高的见证者，如同在信上盖章，让请求更有分量。

senses.title: For its own value alone
senses.titleCN: 就其本身而言（for its own sake）
senses.definition: for its own value without any other purpose, used in for its own sake
senses.definitionCN: 在 for its own sake 中指不为别的目的，只为事物本身
senses.example: He collects stamps for their own sake, not for money.
senses.exampleCN: 他集邮纯粹出于爱好，并非为了钱。
senses.why: When the reason is the thing itself, the weight rests on nothing outside it.
senses.whyCN: 当缘故就是事物本身时，砝码便不再依赖任何外物。

intro.en: Sake comes from Old English sacu, a matter, cause, or dispute, of Germanic origin.
intro.cn: sake 源自古英语 sacu（事由、缘由、争端），属日耳曼语源。

items.en: The Germanic root *sak- meant a matter, a charge, or a legal dispute.
items.cn: 一般认为日耳曼语词根 *sak- 指事情、指控或法律争端，与 seek 同源相关。

items.en: Sacu meant a quarrel, a cause, or a matter at stake.
items.cn: 古英语 sacu 兼指争端、缘由与利害攸关之事。

items.en: Sake narrowed to mean cause or purpose in the phrase for someone's sake.
items.cn: 中古英语时期词义收窄，在 for someone's sake 中专指缘由与目的。

items.en: For God's sake became a fixed emphatic phrase.
items.cn: 十六至十七世纪，for God's sake 固化为加强语气的习语。

items.en: Sake now lives almost entirely inside set phrases.
items.cn: 如今 sake 几乎只活在固定短语之中，单独使用已很少见。

note.en: Sake has look-alike words from the same root and near-meaning words about purpose.
note.cn: sake 的形近词多属同根，近义词集中在目的与缘由义场。

entries.definition: to leave someone or something behind completely
entries.definitionCN: 抛弃；离弃，与 sake 同出古英语 sacu 一族

entries.definition: to move quickly up and down or side to side
entries.definitionCN: 摇动；颤抖，与 sake 仅差首字母，词源无关，只是形近

entries.definition: a large area of water surrounded by land
entries.definitionCN: 湖，与 sake 韵母相同，词源无关，只是形近

entries.definition: an advantage or good result
entries.definitionCN: 益处；好处，指具体收益，sake 多用于固定短语

entries.definition: the reason something happens; a principle one supports
entries.definitionCN: 原因；事业，与 sake 古义相近，今多指原因或事业

entries.definition: advantage or benefit, especially of a group
entries.definitionCN: 利益（尤指群体的），in the interest of 与 for the sake of 相近

normalIntro.en: Five ways to remember sake through reasons and phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕缘由与固定短语的记忆路径。

normal.en: SAKE is the reason that tips the scale of a decision.
normal.cn: SAKE 是让决定的天平倾斜的那颗砝码——缘故。

normal.en: For the SAKE of peace: give a little, gain much.
normal.cn: 为了和平起见：让三分，得全局。

normal.en: For God's SAKE: call the biggest witness to your plea.
normal.cn: for God's sake：请出最大的见证者为请求作保。

normal.en: Art for art's SAKE needs no buyer, no prize.
normal.cn: 为艺术而艺术，不需要买家，也不需要奖项。

normal.en: FORSAKE someone is to leave them for another sake.
normal.cn: forsake（抛弃）一个人，就是「为了别的缘故」离开他。

abstract.en: See one small stone tip a whole balance.
abstract.cn: 看一枚小石子压斜了整架天平。

abstract.en: Hear a sigh before someone agrees for a friend's sake.
abstract.cn: 听一声轻叹——为朋友才勉强答应。

abstract.en: Picture a painter working with no buyer in mind.
abstract.cn: 想象一位画家作画时心中并无买家。

examples.en: Let's not argue for the sake of the project.
examples.cn: 为了项目着想，我们别争了。

examples.en: For safety's sake, everyone must wear a mask here.
examples.cn: 为安全起见，在这里人人都必须戴口罩。

examples.en: He does charity work for its own sake, not for praise.
examples.cn: 他做慈善不为名声，只为这件事本身。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「思意克」——凡事先思其意、克服私心，为了大家起见；sake 读音近似「思意克」

root: 源自古英语 sacu（事由、争端），属日耳曼语词根 *sak-（与 seek 相关）；缘由、目的诸义由「利害攸关之事」收窄而来，今几乎只存于固定短语。

sensesIntro.en: Sake moves from a matter at stake, to the benefit that tips a decision, to emphatic pleas, to things valued for themselves.
sensesIntro.cn: sake 从利害攸关之事出发，到让决定倾斜的利益、加重语气的恳求，再到只为其自身价值之事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a weight on the scale of a decision
core.cn: 核心意象：压在决定天平上的一枚砝码

branches.en: The matter that decides an action is the base image.
branches.cn: 决定行动的缘由是这个词的基础画面。

branches.en: A plea gains force by calling on the greatest sake.
branches.cn: 请出最大的「缘故」，恳求便有了分量。

branches.en: For the sake of names the weight that tips the decision.
branches.cn: for the sake of 说出让决定倾斜的那枚砝码。

branches.en: Some weights rest on nothing outside the thing itself.
branches.cn: 有些砝码不依赖外物，只以事物本身为凭。

branches.en: Forsaking someone means choosing another sake over them.
branches.cn: 抛弃一个人，就是选了别的缘故而舍弃他。

intro.en: Sake lives almost entirely inside set phrases.
intro.cn: sake 几乎只以固定短语的形式存在。

latinIntro.en: Sake is a Germanic word without Latin relatives, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: sake 属日耳曼语源词，没有拉丁同族词，故不列拉丁词条。

items.meaning: for the benefit or purpose of
items.example: He stayed quiet for the sake of peace.
items.exampleCN: 为了息事宁人，他保持了沉默。

items.meaningCN: 看在上帝的份上（表不耐烦）
items.exampleCN: 看在上帝的份上，小心点！

items.example: For heaven's sake, turn the music down.
For safety's sake, check the ladder twice.
items.exampleCN: 为安全起见，梯子要检查两遍。

items.example: They met for old times' sake.
items.exampleCN: 他们为了怀旧之情见了面。

items.meaning: for the value of the thing itself
items.meaningCN: 为事物本身；不为其他目的
items.example: She learns languages for their own sake.
items.exampleCN: 她学语言纯粹出于爱好。

items.meaning: art that needs no other purpose
items.example: The movement believed in art for art's sake.
items.exampleCN: 这一流派信奉为艺术而艺术。

items.example: Never forsake a friend in trouble.
items.exampleCN: 绝不抛弃患难中的朋友。

items.meaningCN: 看在善意的份上（较温和的感叹）

items.meaning: only to follow the proper procedure
items.meaningCN: 为了走形式；例行公事地
items.example: He apologized for form's sake only.

definition_zh: 比率；比值；比例关系
definition_en: the relation between two amounts, showing how many times one contains the other; a proportion between parts
core_image: 天平两端各堆砝码，数目清晰可数的对比
scene: 天平两端各放着一堆砝码，数目一眼就能数清。 The ratio of students to teachers is ten to one.
sceneCN: 这里 ratio 是「比率」（第 1 个义项：两个数量之间的倍数关系）；句意为学生与教师的比例是十比一。画面里可留意：天平两端的砝码、清楚的数目对比。

collocations.phrase: the ratio of A to B
collocations.zh: A 与 B 的比率

derivatives.zh: 与 ratio 同源的拉丁词，指定量、配给
ratio 加 -al，指理性的、合理的
ratio 加 -cin- 与 -ation，指（正式的）推理

senses.title: The relation between two amounts
senses.definition: the relation between two amounts, showing how many times one contains the other
senses.definitionCN: 两个数量之间的关系，表明一个包含另一个多少次
senses.example: The ratio of students to teachers is ten to one.
senses.exampleCN: 学生与教师的比例是十比一。
senses.why: Latin ratio meant a reckoning, and a reckoning of two amounts against each other is exactly a ratio.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ratio 意为计算，而把两个数量相互算一算，正是一个比率。

senses.title: A proportion between parts
senses.definition: a proportion in which parts are compared with one another or with the whole
senses.definitionCN: 各部分相互比较或与整体比较时的比例关系
senses.example: The recipe gives the ratio of flour to water.
senses.exampleCN: 这份食谱给出了面粉与水的比例。
senses.why: Once two amounts could be compared, the word served for any ordered comparison of parts, as in a recipe or a design.
senses.whyCN: 一旦两个数量可以相互比较，这个词便用于任何有次序的部分比较，如食谱或设计中的配比。

intro.en: Ratio is the Latin word for reckoning, calculation and reason; it comes from reri, to reckon or think, and English borrowed it directly.
intro.cn: ratio 是拉丁语中表示计算、推算与理性的词；它源自动词 reri（计算、思考），英语直接借用了它。

items.en: Ratio meant a reckoning or a calculation, and also the faculty of reason that makes counting possible.
items.cn: ratio 意为计算或推算，也指使计数成为可能的理性能力。

items.en: The verb reri meant to reckon or think, and ratio was the noun of that act.
items.cn: 动词 reri 意为计算或思考，ratio 是这一动作的名词。

items.en: Roman writers used ratio for the relation between numbers, the sense that mathematics still keeps.
items.cn: 罗马作者用 ratio 指数字之间的关系，这一意思仍留在数学中。

items.en: English took ratio straight from Latin in the mathematical and general sense of a relation between amounts.
items.cn: 英语直接从拉丁语借入 ratio，用于数学及一般意义上「数量之间的关系」。

items.en: Modern English uses ratio for a quotient, for a proportion between parts, and in fixed phrases such as the golden ratio.
items.cn: 现代英语用 ratio 指比值、部分之间的比例，并见于 golden ratio 等固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin root and one near form; the near-meaning group gathers words for proportion and comparison.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词根的词与一个近形词；近义组收表示比例与比较的词。

entries.definition: A measure or a speed, related in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 一种度量或速度，意义相关。

entries.definition: A fixed share of food or supplies.
entries.definitionCN: 食物或物资的定量份额。

entries.definition: Based on reason.
entries.definitionCN: 基于理性的。

entries.definition: A set of reasons for something.
entries.definitionCN: 为某事给出的一套理由。

entries.definition: The relation of one part to another or to the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 一部分与另一部分或与整体的关系。

entries.definition: A part of a whole, often written as one number over another.
entries.definitionCN: 整体的一部分，常写成一个数在另一个数之上。

entries.definition: A rate or proportion expressed out of a hundred.
entries.definitionCN: 以百为基数表达的比率或比例。

entries.definition: A part given to or held by one person or group.
entries.definitionCN: 给某人或某群体的一份。

normalIntro.en: The word is Latin reckoning, and every sense is a way of putting two amounts side by side to see how they compare.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「计算」，每个义项都是把两个数量并排摆好、看它们如何相比的方式。

normal.en: Ratio and rate both come from reckoning, but ratio compares two amounts while rate measures one against time.
normal.cn: ratio 与 rate 都源于计算，但 ratio 比较两个数量，rate 则用一个量去量时间。

normal.en: The ratio of A to B is written as a pair of numbers, often with a colon.
normal.cn: A 与 B 的比率写成一对数，常用冒号隔开。

normal.en: A recipe works by ratio: so much flour for so much water.
normal.cn: 食谱靠 ratio 运作：多少面粉配多少水。

normal.en: The golden ratio is a fixed proportion that appears in art and nature.
normal.cn: 黄金比例是一个固定的比例，出现在艺术与自然之中。

normal.en: Ration is the same root, a fixed share measured out.
normal.cn: ration 同根，指称量出来的一份定量。

abstract.en: A ratio turns a comparison into a number you can carry away.
abstract.cn: ratio 把一次比较变成一个可以带走的数字。

abstract.en: To give a ratio is to say how much of one thing sits beside another.
abstract.cn: 给出一个 ratio，就是说明一物相对另一物有多少。

abstract.en: Every ratio chooses what to count and what to leave out.
abstract.cn: 每一个 ratio 都在选择数什么、略去什么。

examples.en: The ratio of students to teachers is ten to one.
examples.cn: 学生与教师的比例是十比一。

examples.en: The recipe gives the ratio of flour to water.
examples.cn: 这份食谱给出了面粉与水的比例。

examples.en: Mix the paint in a ratio of two parts blue to one part white.
examples.cn: 按两份蓝配一份白的比例调颜料。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞笑」——天平两端一称，数目比出来了，记住 ratio 是比率、比例。

root: 拉丁语 ratio（计算、理性）→ 英语 ratio；源自动词 reri（计算、思考）。同根有 rate、ration、rational、rationale。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a reckoning of two amounts; the senses divide into a quotient and a proportion between parts.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是对两个数量的计算；义项分为比值与部分之间的比例。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: weights piled on both pans of a balance, their numbers plainly compared.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平两端堆着砝码，数目清楚地相互比较。

chain: TWO AMOUNTS SET SIDE BY SIDE

branches.en: two piles of weights on a balance
branches.cn: 天平上两堆砝码

branches.en: flour and water measured for a recipe
branches.cn: 按食谱量好的面粉与水

branches.en: one quotient and one recipe proportion
branches.cn: 一个比值与一份食谱配比

branches.en: two ways of putting amounts side by side
branches.cn: 把数量并排摆好的两种方式

branches.en: the same reckoning at different scales
branches.cn: 同一套计算在不同尺度上

intro.en: The word is a Latin borrowing, and its family is built with Latin and English suffixes on the root reri.
intro.cn: 这个词借自拉丁语，其词族由 reri 词根上的拉丁语与英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin ratio, a reckoning, and reri, to reckon, are the recorded sources of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ratio（计算）与 reri（计算）是这个词族有记录可考的来源。

definition_zh: 不同；相异；意见不合
definition_en: to be unlike something else, or to hold a different opinion
core_image: 两条并排的路在远处分开，一条进林子，一条通向河边
scene: 两兄弟站在岔路口，一个指左，一个指右。 Their opinions differ sharply on this question.
sceneCN: 这里 differ 指「意见不同」（第 2 个义项：看法不一致）；句意是在这个问题上他们的意见差别很大。

senses.title: To be unlike
senses.definition: to be unlike something else in one or more ways
senses.definitionCN: 在某一方面或几方面与别的东西不一样
senses.example: The two plans differ only in cost.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个方案只在成本上不同。
senses.why: Put two things side by side and a gap shows itself.
senses.whyCN: 把两样东西并排一放，缝隙自己就显出来了。

senses.title: To hold another opinion
senses.definition: to disagree with someone about what should be said or done
senses.definitionCN: 在说什么或做什么上与别人看法不一致
senses.example: Doctors differ about how much exercise is enough.
senses.exampleCN: 医生们对运动多少才算够看法不一。
senses.why: Two people can look at one fact and walk away with two stories.
senses.whyCN: 同一个人事实，两个人看完能带走两套说法。

intro.en: Differ comes from Latin differre, to carry apart, built from dis-, apart, and ferre, to carry.
intro.cn: differ 来自拉丁语 differre，本义是分开搬运，由 dis-（分开）与 ferre（搬、带）构成。

items.en: Ferre meant to carry or to bear a load.
items.cn: ferre 指搬运，也指承担一份重量。

items.en: Differre meant to carry things apart, and so to be unlike.
items.cn: differre 指把东西分开放，因而引申为不同。

items.en: The same verb also meant to put off until later.
items.cn: 同一个动词还表示把事情推到以后。

items.en: English differ took the sense of being unlike and of disagreeing.
items.cn: 英语 differ 承接了「相异」与「意见不合」两层意思。

items.en: The verb now anchors a whole family: difference, different, differentiate.
items.cn: 这个词如今撑起一整族词：difference、different、differentiate。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the diff- shape, while the meaning group covers varying, contrasting and deviating.
note.cn: 形近组共用 diff 这一形状，近义组则覆盖变化、对比与偏离。

entries.definition: to delay something to a later time
entries.definitionCN: 把某事推迟到以后

entries.definition: not the same as another thing
entries.definitionCN: 与另一事物不一样的

entries.definition: based on a difference between groups
entries.definitionCN: 基于群体之间差别的

entries.definition: to change or be different from one case to another
entries.definitionCN: 在个案之间变化或不同

entries.definition: to show a clear difference between two things
entries.definitionCN: 显出两物之间的明显差别

entries.definition: to move away from an expected path or rule
entries.definitionCN: 偏离预期的路线或规则

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with two roads splitting and end with two people reading one fact in two ways.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从两条路分开开始，最后落到两个人把一个事实读成两种。

normal.en: Dis- pulls apart, and ferre carries: differ is to carry apart.
normal.cn: dis- 往两边拉，ferre 是搬：differ 就是把东西搬开。

normal.en: Differ from names the other thing; differ in names the part.
normal.cn: differ from 接另一样东西，differ in 接具体方面。

normal.en: Two clocks differ by a minute and nobody notices for a year.
normal.cn: 两只钟差一分钟，一年都没人发现。

normal.en: To differ is not to fight, though a fight may follow.
normal.cn: differ 不等于争吵，虽然争吵可能跟着来。

normal.en: Different is the adjective, difference is the gap itself.
normal.cn: different 是形容词，difference 是那道缝本身。

abstract.en: Picture two roads leaving one field and never meeting again.
abstract.cn: 想象两条路从同一片田野出发，再没交汇。

abstract.en: Picture two rulers laid side by side, one a little longer.
abstract.cn: 想象两把尺子并排放着，其中一把略长。

abstract.en: Picture two hands pointing at opposite ends of a map.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手分别指着地图的两端。

examples.en: Their answers differ in almost every detail.
examples.cn: 他们的答案几乎每个细节都不同。

examples.en: Opinions differ on whether the plan will work.
examples.cn: 这个方案是否可行，意见并不一致。

examples.en: The twins differ only in the colour of their eyes.
examples.cn: 这对双胞胎只有眼睛的颜色不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 differ 记成「地分」：地一分两边，人就各站一边，于是不同、也不合。

root: 来自拉丁语 differre，由 dis-（分开）与 ferre（搬、带）组成，本义是把东西分开搬运。因为分开之后彼此不再相同，就生出「相异」；又因为各人把话带向不同方向，就生出「意见不合」。同源的 defer 保留了「推后」的古义。

sensesIntro.en: From two things carrying apart, to two minds carrying one question in different directions.
sensesIntro.cn: 从两样东西被搬向两边，到两颗心把同一个问题带向不同方向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two paths that leave the same point and never rejoin.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条路从同一点出发，再没有并回。

chain: TWO MINDS READ THE SAME FACT

branches.en: The first sense is about objects and the gap between them.
branches.cn: 第一个义项说的是东西本身以及它们之间的缝。

branches.en: The second sense moves the gap into people and their views.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把这道缝挪到人以及人的看法里。

branches.en: In both cases something is measured against something else.
branches.cn: 两种情形里，都是拿一样东西去比另一样。

branches.en: Disagreement needs no anger; it only needs two positions.
branches.cn: 分歧不必带火气，只要有两个位置就够了。

branches.en: A difference in facts often turns into a difference in judgment.
branches.cn: 事实上的差别，常常就变成判断上的差别。

intro.en: Differ anchors a large family built on the Latin stem fer-, to carry.
intro.cn: differ 撑起一大族词，词干 fer- 在拉丁语里是「搬、带」。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin ferre, to carry, with dis- meaning apart.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 ferre（搬、带），前缀 dis- 表示分开。

items.meaning: to carry apart, hence to be unlike
items.example: The two versions differ in tone.
The difference is small but real.
Every child learns in a different way.
items.exampleCN: 每个孩子学习的方式都不同。

items.example: He treats his two sons differently.
items.exampleCN: 他对两个儿子的方式不一样。

items.example: A child cannot differentiate the two sounds.

items.exampleCN: 细胞分化要经过许多步骤。

items.example: She was indifferent to the result.
His indifference hurt her more than anger.
items.exampleCN: 他的冷淡比发火更伤她。

definition_zh: 搅拌；搅动；（使）微动；激起；轰动；唤醒
definition_en: to move a liquid around with a spoon, or to wake a feeling and make people excited
core_image: 一把勺子画圈搅开沉底的糖——糖粒旋起，水面生涡
scene: 周末早晨，奶奶在灶台前煮麦片粥。 She stirred the porridge slowly so it would not burn at the bottom.
sceneCN: 这里 stir 是动词「搅拌」（第 1 个义项：用勺使液体转动）；句意为她慢慢搅着麦片粥，免得糊底。

pos.zh: 动词：搅拌；搅动；激起；（使）微动

derivatives.zh: 由本词现在分词转作形容词，义为「激动人心的」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「搅拌棒；搬弄是非者」
由本词加复合成分构成，义为「翻炒」

senses.title: To move a liquid or mixture around with a tool
senses.definition: to turn a spoon or similar tool round and round in a liquid or mixture
senses.definitionCN: 用勺子等工具在液体或混合物中画圈转动
senses.example: Stir the paint well before you start.
senses.exampleCN: 开刷之前把油漆搅匀。
senses.why: The spoon draws circles and lifts what has settled at the bottom.
senses.whyCN: 勺子画圈，把沉底的糖粒旋起，即搅拌。

senses.title: To move slightly, or begin to wake
senses.definition: to make a small movement, or begin to become active after sleep or rest
senses.definitionCN: 轻微移动，或在睡眠、休息后开始活动起来
senses.example: The baby stirred just before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天快亮时婴儿动了一下。
senses.why: The settled sugar shivers before the whirl forms.
senses.whyCN: 涡流成形前，沉底的糖粒先轻轻一颤，即微动。

senses.title: To wake a feeling or make people excited
senses.definition: to make feelings, memories, or interest become active
senses.definitionCN: 使情感、回忆或兴趣活跃起来
senses.example: The old song stirred memories of her hometown.
senses.exampleCN: 这首老歌唤起了她对故乡的回忆。
senses.why: The spoon reaches down and lifts what lay still inside.
senses.whyCN: 勺子探到底，把沉在心里的东西旋起，即唤起。

senses.title: Excitement spreading among people
senses.definition: a state of excitement or interest spreading through a group, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 在人群中蔓延的兴奋或关注，作名词使用
senses.example: The new policy caused a stir in the press.
senses.exampleCN: 新政策在媒体界引起轰动。
senses.why: One spoon-stroke and the whole pot turns together.
senses.whyCN: 一勺搅下，整锅水一起转动，即群体骚动。

intro.en: Stir is an Old English word for moving or troubling something, from a Germanic root of agitating.
intro.cn: stir 源自古英语，指搅动、扰动，一般认为出自日耳曼语「使翻动」词根。

items.en: A reconstructed root *stur- is thought to mean to agitate or disturb.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *stur- 意为翻搅、扰动。

items.en: Styrian meant to move, trouble, or disturb something.
items.cn: 古英语 styrian 意为移动、搅扰某物。

items.en: Stiren covered stirring food, waking, and being roused to action.
items.cn: 中古英语 stiren 兼指搅动食物、醒来与被激起行动。

items.en: The emotional and public senses grew: stirring speeches, a stir in town.
items.cn: 情感与公众义发展：激动人心的演说、城中的轰动。

items.en: Stir-fry entered from Chinese cooking, and stir-crazy named restless confinement.
items.cn: stir-fry 经中餐进入英语，stir-crazy 形容被关得发闷。

note.en: Stir looks like the unrelated star, and sits near mixing words of different roots.
note.cn: stir 拼写上与不相关的 star 相近，义场靠近词源不同的混合词。

entries.definition: a burning ball of gas in the sky, or a famous person
entries.definitionCN: 星星；明星；与 stir 只差一个字母，词源不同

entries.definition: a metal loop for the foot when riding a horse
entries.definitionCN: 马镫；拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: exciting strong feelings
entries.definitionCN: 激动人心的；由 stir 派生的形容词

entries.definition: to combine things so they blend together
entries.definitionCN: 混合；掺和，强调合并为一体

entries.definition: to beat quickly with a wire tool
entries.definitionCN: 搅打；用打蛋器快速搅，比 stir 更猛

entries.definition: to wake someone or make them active
entries.definitionCN: 唤醒；激起，对应 stir 的唤醒义

entries.definition: to make peaceful and still
entries.definitionCN: 使平静；安抚，与搅动相反

normalIntro.en: The spoon-circle image serves cooking, waking, and public excitement alike.
normalIntro.cn: 勺子画圈的画面同时服务烹调、唤醒与公众骚动。

normal.en: Stir, stirred, stirred is the regular verb chain.
normal.cn: stir—stirred—stirred 是规则动词变化链。

normal.en: Stir up trouble and stir up memories share one phrase.
normal.cn: stir up trouble 与 stir up memories 共用 stir up 短语。

normal.en: Cause a stir means to attract excited public attention.
normal.cn: cause a stir 指引起公众的热切关注。

normal.en: Stir-fry is the kitchen word for cooking quickly in oil.
normal.cn: stir-fry 是大火快炒的厨房用语。

normal.en: Not stir an inch is an idiom for refusing to move.
normal.cn: not stir an inch 表示一动不动、拒绝挪步。

abstract.en: Watch sugar crystals spiral up from the bottom of a glass.
abstract.cn: 看糖粒从杯底旋升而起。

abstract.en: Feel a sleeping town stir as its first lights come on.
abstract.cn: 感受沉睡的小镇随第一盏灯亮而苏醒。

abstract.en: Hear a speech whose words lift a whole hall together.
abstract.cn: 听一场让全场一起沸腾的演讲。

examples.en: He stirred his coffee and read the morning paper.
examples.cn: 他搅了搅咖啡，读起晨报。

examples.en: The film stirred deep feelings in the audience.
examples.cn: 这部电影激起了观众深深的情感。

examples.en: The court ruling caused a stir across the country.
examples.cn: 法院裁决在全国引起轰动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯特」——谐音「死特（搅）」：勺子死命画圈特搅，糖粒全起来。

root: 源自古英语 styrian（搅动、扰动），一般认为上溯至日耳曼语 *stur-（翻搅）；与 star、stirrup 无词源关系。

sensesIntro.en: The spoon-circle gives the mixing hand, the small shiver of waking, the lifted feeling, and the pot-wide excitement of a crowd.
sensesIntro.cn: 勺圈给出搅动的手、初醒的微颤、被旋起的情感，以及满锅般的人群骚动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spoon drawing circles that lift the settled sugar
core.cn: 核心意象：勺子画圈，旋起沉底的糖粒

branches.en: the mixing hand at work
branches.cn: 搅拌之手

branches.en: the first shiver before motion
branches.cn: 动作前的轻微一颤

branches.en: feelings lifted from their rest
branches.cn: 被旋起的情感

branches.en: a whole group turning at once
branches.cn: 群体同时转动

branches.en: waking from sleep and from silence
branches.cn: 从睡眠与沉默中苏醒

intro.en: Stir grows cooking compounds and feeling words with ease.
intro.cn: stir 轻松衍生出烹饪复合词与情感词。

latinIntro.en: Stir has no Latin relatives; it is native Germanic, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: stir 没有拉丁同源词，属日耳曼本土词源，故拉丁同族词列表为空。

items.meaning: exciting strong feeling; the action of mixing
a tool or person that stirs
makes nouns for tools or doers
items.meaningCN: 名词后缀，表工具或施动者

items.meaning: restless from being shut in too long

derivatives.zh: 由本词现在分词转作形容词，义为「激动人心的」
由本词加名词后缀 -er 构成，义为「搅拌棒；搬弄是非者」
由本词加复合成分 fry 构成，义为「翻炒」

definition_zh: 发生；出现；存在；被想到；在文中出现
definition_en: to happen, to present itself, to be found somewhere, or to come into the mind
core_image: 两样东西在同一条路上迎面跑来，一头撞上
scene: 夜班时，冷却系统里出现了一处故障。 A fault occurred in the cooling system during the night shift.
sceneCN: 这里 occur 是「发生、出现」（第 2 个义项：事件发生）；句意：夜班期间冷却系统出现了故障。图中可辨识物件：亮起的警报灯、冷却管道、值班人员、夜班记录本；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 发生；出现；存在；（想法）浮现

derivatives.zh: 正在发生的；偶然发生的

senses.title: Run to meet: the Latin core sense
senses.titleCN: 迎面跑去：拉丁语的本义
senses.definition: in the original Latin sense, to run toward something and meet it, including meeting an opponent in argument
senses.definitionCN: 按拉丁语本义，跑向某物并与之相遇，也包括在争论中迎上对手
senses.example: Latin occurrere described two people or things running toward each other until they met.
senses.exampleCN: 拉丁语 occurrere 描述两方在奔跑中相互靠近，直到碰上。
senses.why: Latin occurrere joined ob 'against, toward' to currere 'to run'. The first picture is a head-on meeting, not an accident and not a thought.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 occurrere 把 ob“迎着、朝着”与 currere“跑”组合起来。最初的画面是迎面相遇，既不是事故，也不是念头。

senses.title: Happen: take place
senses.definition: to happen, especially without being planned or looked for
senses.definitionCN: 发生，尤指并非计划之中或特意寻找的
senses.example: The accident occurred at the crossroads just after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 事故就发生在午夜过后的十字路口。
senses.why: From 'meet' the word moved to 'present itself in the course of events'. An event that meets you on the road is an event that happens to you.
senses.whyCN: 从“相遇”出发，这个词转向“在事件进程中自己浮现”。在路上迎上你的事，就是发生在你身上的事。

senses.title: Happen at a stated time or place
senses.definition: to take place at a particular point in time or in a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 在特定的时间点或特定地点发生
senses.example: The festival occurs in the first week of June.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节日在六月的第一周举行。
senses.why: Once an event is pictured as meeting you, it can be pinned to a spot on the road and a moment on the clock.
senses.whyCN: 一旦事件被想象成与你相遇，它就能被钉在路上的某个地点和时钟上的某个时刻。

senses.title: Be found to exist: occur in nature
senses.titleCN: 存在于某处：自然界里有它
senses.definition: to be found or to exist in a place, a group, or a natural setting
senses.definitionCN: 在某地、某群体或自然环境中被发现、存在
senses.example: This orchid occurs only in the high wetlands of the north.
senses.exampleCN: 这种兰花只生长在北部的髙地湿地。
senses.why: If a thing presents itself when you go looking, it 'occurs' there: the meeting becomes a record of where it can be met.
senses.whyCN: 如果去找就能遇见，它就是“occur”在那里：相遇变成了“何处能遇见它”的记录。

senses.title: Appear in a text or a list
senses.definition: to appear in a piece of writing, a list, or a set of data
senses.definitionCN: 出现在文章、名单或一组数据中
senses.example: The word 'harbour' occurs four times in the first paragraph.
senses.exampleCN: harbour 这个词在第一段出现了四次。
senses.why: A page is a road too: the reader runs along it, and every word that meets the eye 'occurs' at that point.
senses.whyCN: 书页也是一条路：读者沿着它跑，每一个撞进眼睛的词就在那一点“occur”。

senses.title: Come into the mind: occur to someone
senses.definition: in the pattern occur to someone, of an idea: to come into a person's mind
senses.definitionCN: 用于 occur to someone 结构，指想法进入某人脑中
senses.example: It never occurred to me to check the date on the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 我从没想到要去核对信上的日期。
senses.why: The 1620s added the mental branch: a thought runs toward you and meets you, seemingly from outside, which is why English says the idea occurred rather than 'I thought it'.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 20 年代增加了心理分支：一个念头朝你跑来并遇上你，好像来自外部，所以英语说“想法 occur 了”，而不是“我想到了它”。

senses.title: Exist in a particular form or variety
senses.definition: to exist in a particular form, type, or variety, often one of several
senses.definitionCN: 以某种形态、类型或变体存在，常是若干种之一
senses.example: The mineral occurs in two distinct crystal forms.
senses.exampleCN: 这种矿物以两种不同的晶体形态存在。
senses.why: The 'be met with' sense narrows to how a thing is met: the form it presents when you encounter it.
senses.whyCN: “能被遇见”的义项收窄为“以何种样子被遇见”：你碰到它时它呈现的形态。

senses.title: Occur to someone to do: an idea that prompts action
senses.titleCN: 想到要去做：推动行动的念头
senses.definition: in the pattern it occurs to someone to do something, of an idea that suggests an action
senses.definitionCN: 用于 「it occurs to someone to do something」 结构，指想到该做某事
senses.example: It occurred to her to call the police before leaving.
senses.exampleCN: 她离开前想到该报警。
senses.why: The mental meeting can carry a plan as well as a fact: what meets the mind is not only 'that something is so' but 'that something should be done'.
senses.whyCN: 心理上的相遇既能带来事实，也能带来计划：撞进脑子的不只是“事情如此”，还有“应该去做”。

intro.en: Occur entered English in the 1520s meaning 'meet, meet in argument', from Latin occurrere 'run to meet'. The sense 'happen' and the mental sense 'come into the mind' followed within a century.
intro.cn: occur 于 16 世纪 20 年代进入英语，意为“相遇、在争论中迎上”，来自拉丁语 occurrere“跑去相遇”。“发生”义与“想到”义在一个世纪内相继出现。

items.en: First recorded meaning 'meet, meet in argument', with the physical head-on meeting still visible in the word.
items.cn: 最早记录为“相遇、在争论中迎上”，词里仍看得见那种物理性的迎面相遇。

items.en: From French occurrer 'happen unexpectedly', or directly from Latin occurrere.
items.cn: 来自法语 occurrer“意外发生”，或直接来自拉丁语 occurrere。

items.en: Latin occurrere 'run to meet, run against, befall, present itself' is ob 'against, toward' plus currere 'to run'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 occurrere“跑去相遇、迎面撞上、降临、自己出现”由 ob“迎着、朝向”加 currere“跑”构成。

items.en: Currere goes back to PIE *kers- 'to run', the root also seen in current and excursion.
items.cn: currere 追溯到原始印欧语 *kers-“跑”，current 与 excursion 也出自这个词根。

items.en: The noun occurrence is recorded from the 1530s; the sense 'come into one's mind' appears in the 1620s.
items.cn: 名词 occurrence 自 16 世纪 30 年代有记录；“想到”义出现于 17 世纪 20 年代。

items.en: Modern English keeps the event sense as the main one and leaves the literal meeting to the root; occurrence, co-occur and recur carry the family forward.
items.cn: 现代英语以事件义为主，把字面的“相遇”留在词根里；occurrence、co-occur、recur 延续了这个词族。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: to fill space, time or attention. It shares oc-/ob- and the -py ending shape but comes from capere 'to grasp', not currere 'to run'.
entries.definitionCN: 占据空间、时间或注意力。它形似 occur，但词根是 capere“抓”，不是 currere“跑”。

entries.definition: an event, or the fact of something happening. It is the noun from occur, not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: 事件；发生。它是 occur 派生的名词，不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: to happen again. It uses re- 'again' plus the same currere 'to run' root.
entries.definitionCN: 再次发生。它用 re-“再次”加同一个 currere“跑”词根。

entries.definition: to take place, usually by chance. It is the plain everyday word, while occur is more formal and often written.
entries.definitionCN: 发生，通常带偶然意味。它是最平实的日常词，occur 更正式，多用于书面。

entries.definition: to happen or become known. It is formal and often suggests that facts emerged gradually.
entries.definitionCN: 发生；逐渐为人所知。它偏正式，常暗示事实慢慢显露。

entries.definition: to come into being, especially of problems or situations. It points to a source, while occur only records that something took place.
entries.definitionCN: 产生，尤指问题或局面。它指向来源，occur 只记录某事发生了。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin ob plus currere, the currere family in current and excursion, and the fixed pattern occur to someone.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁成分 ob + currere，current 与 excursion 中的 currere 词族，以及固定结构 occur to someone。

normal.en: ob 'toward' plus currere 'to run' gives 'run to meet': something comes at you and you meet it.
normal.cn: ob“朝向”加 currere“跑”就是“跑去相遇”：有东西朝你而来，你与它撞上。

normal.en: Current, excursion, concur and recur all share currere 'to run', the root that makes occur a meeting.
normal.cn: current、excursion、concur、recur 都含 currere“跑”，正是这个词根让 occur 成为一次相遇。

normal.en: Obtain uses tenere 'to hold' and occupy uses capere 'to grasp': the same ob- prefix, three different roots.
normal.cn: obtain 用 tenere“握持”，occupy 用 capere“抓”：同一个 ob- 前缀，三个不同词根。

normal.en: It never occurred to me is the mental branch: the idea runs up to you from outside.
normal.cn: it never occurred to me 是心理分支：念头从外面跑到你面前。

normal.en: Occurrence, co-occur and recur are the everyday nouns and verbs built on the same stem.
normal.cn: occurrence、co-occur、recur 是由同一词干构成的日常名词和动词。

abstract.en: Picture two runners on one road, each heading straight for the other: that collision is the original occur.
abstract.cn: 想象同一条路上两个奔跑的人，各自直冲对方：那次相撞就是 occur 的原型。

abstract.en: An event can run at you the same way, which is why a fault or an accident 'occurs' rather than simply being there.
abstract.cn: 事件也能以同样的方式朝你跑来，所以故障或事故是“occur”，而不只是“在那里”。

abstract.en: A thought can run at you too: it appears from outside, meets the mind, and is reported as occurred.
abstract.cn: 念头也会朝你跑来：它从外面出现，撞上你的心，被说成“occur 了”。

examples.en: Most errors in the survey occurred where the form was printed in two columns.
examples.cn: 问卷中的大多数错误发生在表格排成两栏的地方。

examples.en: It occurred to him only later that the key had been left in the door.
examples.cn: 他后来才想到钥匙被留在了门上。

examples.en: These fish occur in every river along the coast.
examples.cn: 这种鱼在沿海每条河里都有分布。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，扣儿」——哦，扣儿！扣子突然掉了，事情就这样发生了 → occur 发生、出现

root: 源自拉丁语 occurrere“跑去相遇、迎面撞上”= ob-“迎着、朝向”+ currere“跑”（PIE *kers-“跑”），核心是“朝你跑来并撞见”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of occur all start from one picture: something runs toward you on the same road. The meeting then becomes an event, a location, a line in a text, a form in nature, and finally an idea that arrives in the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: occur 的八个义项都从同一幅画出发：有东西在同一条路上朝你跑来。那次相遇随后变成事件、地点、文本里的一行、自然界中的一种形态，最后变成抵达脑中的念头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something running toward you on the same road until it meets you.
core.cn: 核心意象：有东西在同一条路上朝你跑来，直到与你相遇。

branches.en: THE LITERAL MEETING: the Latin head-on encounter, including meeting an opponent in argument.
branches.cn: 字面的相遇：拉丁语里的迎面撞见，也包括争论中迎上对手。

branches.en: THE EVENT: what presents itself in the course of things, and can be pinned to a time and place.
branches.cn: 事件：在事情进程中自己出现的东西，可以被钉在某个时间与地点。

branches.en: THE FOUND THING: where a species or mineral can be met, and in what form it presents itself.
branches.cn: 被遇见之物：物种或矿物能在何处遇到，以及它以什么形态出现。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN PAGE: the road becomes a text, and each word meets the reader at a point.
branches.cn: 书页：路变成文本，每个词在某个位置与读者相遇。

branches.en: THE MIND: an idea runs up to you, either as a fact noticed or as an action suggested.
branches.cn: 心念：念头跑到你面前，或者作为一个被注意到的事实，或者作为一件该做的事。

intro.en: Occur is Latin ob- 'toward, against' plus currere 'to run', with the verb ending -ere. English keeps the stem occurr- and adds -ence, -ent and the prefixes co- and re-.
intro.cn: occur 由拉丁语 ob-“迎着、朝向”加 currere“跑”和动词词尾 -ere 构成。英语保留词干 occurr-，并加 -ence、-ent 以及前缀 co-、re-。

latinIntro.en: The direct source is Latin occurrere, from ob and currere; currere 'to run' is the root shared by current, course and excursion.
latinIntro.cn: 直接来源是拉丁语 occurrere，由 ob 与 currere 构成；currere“跑”是 current、course、excursion 共有的词根。

items.meaning: to run to meet; to present itself, happen, or come to mind
items.meaningCN: 迎面相遇；出现；发生；想到
items.example: The same problem occurs in every third sample.
items.exampleCN: 每三个样本中就有一个出现同样的问题。

items.meaning: the fact of happening, or an event that happens
items.meaningCN: 发生；发生的事件（-ence 构成名词）
items.example: Power cuts are a weekly occurrence here.

items.meaning: happening at a particular time; incidental
items.meaningCN: 正在发生的；偶然发生的（-ent 构成形容词）
items.example: The occurrent noise came from the lift shaft.
items.exampleCN: 当时那阵声响来自电梯井。

items.meaning: to happen or appear at the same time
items.meaningCN: 同时发生；共现（co- 表“共同”）
items.example: Rain and strong wind often co-occur in this valley.
items.exampleCN: 在这个山谷里，降雨和大风常常同时出现。

items.meaning: to run back again, hence to happen once more
items.meaningCN: 再次发生；复发（re-“再次”+ currere“跑”）
items.exampleCN: 疼痛每年春天都会复发。

items.example: Doctors watch for a recurrence of the tumour.
items.exampleCN: 医生密切留意肿瘤是否复发。

items.meaning: running or flowing now; a flow of water or power
items.example: The current carries the boat downstream.

items.meaning: a running out, hence a short journey
items.meaningCN: 远足；短途旅行（ex-“出”+ currere“跑”）
items.example: The class took a one-day excursion to the coast.
items.exampleCN: 全班去海边做了一日短途旅行。

items.meaning: to run together, hence to agree or happen at once
items.meaningCN: 同时发生；同意（con-“共同”+ currere“跑”）
items.example: Both experts concur with the report's conclusion.
items.exampleCN: 两位专家都同意报告的结论。

items.meaning: to run into something, hence to bring upon oneself
items.meaningCN: 招致；蒙受（in-“进入”+ currere“跑”，即“撞上”）
items.example: Late payment will incur a fine.

latinEntries.meaning: to run to meet, run against, befall, present itself
latinEntries.meaningCN: 跑去相遇；迎面撞上；降临；自己出现
